Thus, the Great **World** <note>The Macrocosm or the universe.</note> shall be thoroughly replenished by the generation of the lesser <note>The Microcosm, referring here to the alchemical "offspring" or the stone itself.</note>, which may abundantly possess the Celestial Kingdom of the Creator.

But to whomever the Omnipotent God gives the gift of knowledge, to him it is evident enough and clearly written—indeed, more clearly than can be believed. I have described the whole process figuratively and in the philosophical manner, just as my predecessors have done. In fact, I have spoken more plainly than they did, for I have concealed nothing. If you remove the veil from your eyes, you shall find that which many have sought and few find; for the Matter <note>The *Prima Materia*, or the essential starting substance of the Alchemical Work.</note> is absolutely expressed by its name, and its beginning, middle, and end are also demonstrated.

## The Twelfth Key.

---

**A** fencer who knows not how to use his weapon <note>original: "uſe his weapon"</note> can gain no advantage from it, because he has not rightly learned its use; if another who understands it better than he does fights with him, the unskillful fencer must necessarily be beaten.

<note>The Twelfth Key typically focuses on the "Fermentation" or the final perfection of the Philosopher's Stone. The analogy of the fencer suggests that even with the correct materials, a lack of "skill"—or precise laboratory technique—will lead to failure when compared to a master alchemist.</note>

<summary>This page introduces the Twelfth Key through an analogy of a fencer, emphasizing that theoretical possession of a "weapon" (alchemical knowledge or materials) is useless without the practical skill to use it correctly.</summary>
<keywords>Basil Valentine, Twelfth Key, alchemy, fencer, skill, practice, mastery</keywords>

...beaten by him. He who has well-attained the mastery of the fencing school wins the prize.

So he who has, by the grace of the omnipotent God, obtained the <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tincture"; in alchemy, a potent substance or "elixir" capable of transmuting base metals into gold or healing the body</note> and does not know how to use it—it happens to him as was said of the fencer who did not know the use of his weapon. But seeing this twelfth and last Key is for the finishing of my book, I will no longer detain you with parabolical or figurative expressions. Instead, without any obscurity, I will reveal this Key of the <term>tincture</term> in a most perfect and true process. Therefore, observe my teaching as follows:

When the <term>medicine</term> and <term>Philosophers' Stone</term> <note>the legendary substance that alchemists believed could turn lead into gold and grant eternal life</note> is made and perfectly prepared out of the true <term>virgin's milk</term> <note>original: "Virgins Milk"; a symbolic term for a specific mercurial solvent used in the early stages of the Great Work</note>, take one part of it and three parts of the best and purest <term>gold</term> (melted and purified by <term>antimony</term>). Reduce this gold into plates as thin as you possibly can. Put these together into a <term>crucible</term> <note>a ceramic or metal container used for melting substances at very high temperatures</note> of the kind you use to melt metals. First, apply a gentle fire for twelve hours, then let it stand for three days and nights continually in a melting fire. Then, the pure <term>gold</term> and the <term>stone</term> are made into a simple <term>medicine</term> of a subtle, spiritual, and penetrating quality. 

For without the <term>ferment</term> <note>an "yeast" or catalyst used to stabilize and direct the power of the alchemical stone</note> of <term>gold</term>, the <term>stone</term> cannot operate or exercise its coloring quality, as it is too subtle and penetrative. But once it is fermented and united with its similar <term>ferment</term>, the prepared <term>tincture</term> gains the ability to enter and act upon other bodies. Then, take one part of the prepared <term>ferment</term> for every thousand parts of melted metal you wish to color; know for a very certain truth that it shall be transmuted into good and fixed <term>gold</term>. For the one body embraces the other, although they be not...

### OF THE
# FIRST MATTER
### OF THE
# PHILOSOPHERS STONE.

*A stone is found which is considered lowly <note>original: "vile"</note>,*
*From which is drawn a volatile fire.*
*From which our noble Stone itself is made,*
*Composed of white and red that never will fade.*
*It is called a stone, and yet is no stone;*
*And in that stone, Lady Nature <note>original: "Dame Nature"</note> works alone.*
*The fountain that once flowed from it*
*Has also drowned its fixed father.* <note>In alchemy, a "fixed" substance is one that is stable and does not evaporate when heated, whereas "volatile" substances are easily evaporated.</note>
*His life and body are both devoured,*
*Until at last his soul is restored to him:*
*And his volatile mother is made one,*
*And made equal with him in his own kingdom.*
*He himself has also gained virtue and power,*
*And attained far greater strength than before.*
*In old age, the son also excels*
*His own mother, who is made volatile*
*By Vulcan’s art <note>Vulcan’s art: A common alchemical term referring to the use of fire and the furnace to transform matter.</note>; but first it is thus indeed:*
*The father must proceed from the spirit.*
*Body, soul, and spirit are contained in two,*
*The whole Art <note>The "Art" refers to the Great Work (Magnum Opus) of alchemy.</note> may well be gained from them.*

**Adam** <note>In alchemical symbolism, "Adam" typically refers to the "Red Man" or Sulfur, representing the active, masculine principle of the Great Work.</note> resides in a **Bath** <note>original: *Balneo*; a "bain-marie" or warm water bath used for gentle, indirect heating in a laboratory.</note>

## The XII Keys.

I, *Basilius Valentinus*, a monk of the Order of Saint *Benedict* <note>original: "Bennet"</note>, have written a small treatise and, like the ancients, have revealed in a philosophical manner how that most excellent treasure may be attained, by which the true philosophers greatly prolonged their lives.

And although my conscience bears witness before the Highest in the Heavens—to whom all secrets are manifest—that I have written no untruths, I have made the truth itself so plain that men of understanding need no further light. (For my theory written for them, which was confirmed and made plain by the practice <note>original: "practick"</note> of the twelve keys, is sufficient.) Nevertheless, the restlessness of my mind, through my various reflections <note>original: "cogitations"</note>, worked upon me so much that I undertook to add this small tract. My goal is to demonstrate a shorter way and, as it were, to purify that burning light by this means, so that every lover of true wisdom may have their desire more fully realized by that splendor and clarity. 

And although many consider it clear enough already—and thus heap the burden of many complaints <note>original: "evils"</note> upon me—let everyone know that those who are dull of understanding will find what they seek to be difficult enough. However, to the adept <note>original: "adepted"</note>, it will be plain and easy. Therefore, you who search for truth, attend to my instructions, and you shall find the true way to the Art <note>In this context, "Art" refers specifically to Alchemy.</note>.

For I have written nothing except that which I shall bear witness to after my death and at the resurrection of my body.

<summary>Basilius Valentinus introduces a supplemental tract to his "Twelve Keys," asserting that while his previous work was truthful and sufficient, he wishes to provide a shorter, clearer path to the alchemical "Art" for those of true understanding.</summary>
<keywords>Basilius Valentinus, alchemy, Order of Saint Benedict, Twelve Keys, the Art, philosophical treasure, resurrection</keywords>

# The XII Keys

You will faithfully and truly find the shorter way in the following discourse, for my sayings are founded on simplicity and not on deceptive <note>original: "Sophistical Expressions"; referring to intentionally complex or misleading language used by some alchemical writers</note> phrasing.

I have mentioned and demonstrated that all things are made and composed of three essences, namely Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt; and what I have said is true.

But know this: the Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> is made of one, two, three, four, and five.
* **Five** refers to the quintessence <note>The "fifth essence" or the purest, most concentrated form of matter</note> of its substance.
* **Four** refers to the four elements <note>Earth, Air, Fire, and Water</note>.
* **Three** refers to the three principles of all things <note>Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt</note>.
* **Two** refers to the double mercurial substance.
* **One** refers to the First Essence <note>original: "Ens primum"</note> of all things, which flowed from the command <note>original: "Fiat"; the divine word of creation</note> of the first Creation.

Many well-intentioned artists <note>In this context, "artists" refers to alchemists or practitioners of the "Great Work"</note> may be doubtful of attaining the foundation and understanding of the following discoveries. Therefore, I will first speak very briefly of Mercury; secondly, of Sulfur; and thirdly, of Salt; for these are the essences of the matter of our Stone.

First, know that no common quicksilver <note>original: "Argent vive"</note> is fit for our use. Rather, our quicksilver is made from the best metal by the <term>Spagyric Art</term> <note>The alchemical process of separating and then recombining the constituents of a substance to purify it</note>. It is pure, subtle, clear, and radiant as a fountain, transparent as crystal, and without any impurity. From this, make a water or an incombustible oil; for Mercury was originally water, as all philosophers <note>Alchemical authorities and sages</note> agree with my teaching and doctrine.

In this mercurial oil, dissolve its own mercury—the same from which the water was made—and precipitate that mercury with its own oil. Then you will have a double mercurial substance. Know also that your gold must first be dissolved in a certain water,

And the volatile blood makes the fixed blood volatile, and the fixed likewise makes the volatile blood fixed, as it was before its dissolution. ### *I will also give you my opinion of the Salt of the Philosophers.*

**S**alt makes substances fixed or volatile, according to the degree in which it is ordered and prepared. For the Spirit of Salt of Tartar <note>a substance derived from the potassium bitartrate deposits in wine barrels</note>, if it is distilled *by itself* <note>original: per se</note> and without addition, makes all metals volatile through dissolution and putrefaction; it resolves them into a true "living" <note>original: Vive</note> or liquid mercury, as my practical doctrine demonstrates.

Salt of Tartar *by itself* fixes substances most firmly, especially if the heat of quicklime <note>original: Calx Vive; calcium oxide</note> is incorporated with it, for both of these have a remarkable power of fixing <note>i.e., making a substance resistant to heat so it does not evaporate</note>.

So also the vegetable Salt of Wine both fixes and makes substances volatile according to its various preparations and as its use requires; this is certainly a great mystery of Nature and a wonder of the Philosophical Art <note>i.e., alchemy</note>.

If a man drinks wine, and from his urine a clear salt is made, that salt is volatile and makes other fixed things volatile, carrying them over the "helm" <note>the head or cap of a distilling apparatus</note> with it, but it does not fix them. And although the man drinks nothing but wine, the salt produced from his urine has different properties than the Salt of Tartar or the dregs <note>original: Feces</note> of wine. This is because a transmutation occurs within the human body, so that from a vegetable <note>meaning plant-based</note> substance, that is,

# The Twelve Keys

Just as out of a spirit of wine, an animal spirit of salt is made, and horses—through the strengthening of their natural virtue <note>original: "vertue"; refers to the inherent power or life force of the animal</note>—transmute oats, hay, and similar things and convert them into fat and flesh, so does the bee make honey out of the best flowers and herbs.

Understand other things in the same way: This Key and cause consist only in putrefaction <note>The process of decay or breakdown, considered by alchemists to be essential for the separation and transformation of matter</note>, which is the source of such separation and transmutation.

The spirit of common salt <note>Hydrochloric acid</note>, which is drawn in a peculiar manner, makes gold and silver volatile. If a small quantity of the spirit of the *Dragon* <note>In alchemical symbolism, the "Dragon" often refers to mercury or a strong mineral acid</note> is added to it, it dissolves the metal and carries it over with it *through an alembic* <note>original: "per Alembicum"; a distillation apparatus consisting of two retorts connected by a tube</note>. The *Eagle* <note>Often symbolizing sal ammoniac or mercury</note> does the same with the *Dragon's* spirit, which dwells in stony places. But if anything is melted with salt before the spirit is separated from its body, it fixes the substance much more than it makes it volatile.

I tell you further, if the spirit of common salt is united with the spirit of wine <note>Alcohol</note>, and both are distilled together three times, then it grows sweet and loses its sharpness <note>original: "acrimony"</note>. This prepared spirit does not physically dissolve gold; but if it is poured on a prepared calx of gold <note>A powder or oxide produced by roasting a metal</note>, it extracts its highest tincture <note>The essence or concentrated color/power of a substance</note> and redness. If this is done rightly, it restores pure and white *Luna* <note>Silver</note> into the same color its body had before it was extracted. Also, the old body will again attain its color by the love of enticing *Venus* <note>Copper</note>, being descended from the same origin, state, and blood—though this is not the place to speak further of that.

Know also that the spirit of salt destroys *Luna* <note>Silver</note> and reduces it into a spiritual essence, according to my instruction, from which...

# Thanks be unto God.

**F**or a conclusion to this appendix, I must tell you that from black *Saturn* <term>Lead</term> and friendly *Jove* <term>Tin</term>, a spirit may be extracted which is afterwards reduced into a sweet oil as its noblest part. This medicine, specifically <note>original: *particulariter*</note>, absolutely removes the nimble, running quality from common *Mercury* <term>Quicksilver</term> and brings it to an improvement <note>original: "melioration"</note>, just as I taught you before.

---

->A N<-

# A D D I T I O N.

**H**aving thus obtained the Matter, nothing remains except that you watch the fire well and observe its regulation <note>original: "Regiment", meaning the management of the heat</note>. For in this is the highest importance and the end of the work. Our fire is a common fire, and our furnace is a common furnace. Although those who came before me have written that our fire is not a common fire, I tell you in truth that they concealed all mysteries in their own way. They did this because the Matter is common <note>original: "vile", meaning cheap or base</note> and the work itself is slight, which is only advanced and revealed through the regulation of the fire.

# The XII Keys
<page-num>287</page-num>

The fire of a lamp fueled with <term>alcohol</term> <note>original: Spirit of Wine</note> is useless, and the cost of it would be unbelievable. Horse dung <note>original: *Fimus Equinus*</note> spoils the process, for it cannot complete the work using the correct degrees of heat.

Many and various furnaces are not necessary, for in our <term>threefold furnace</term> <note>A specialized alchemical furnace designed to provide varying levels of heat (such as evaporation, sublimation, and calcination) in a single structure.</note> only the specific degrees of fire are properly maintained. Therefore, do not let any babbling <term>sophister</term> <note>A deceptive or fallacious reasoner; in this context, someone who pretends to have alchemical knowledge they do not possess.</note> lead you into error with the use of many different furnaces. Just as our furnace is common, so is our fire common; and as our matter is common, so is our glass vessel compared to the globe of the Earth. You need no further instructions concerning the fire, its <term>regiment</term> <note>The systematic management or regulation of heat levels during the process.</note>, or the furnace.

For he who has the matter will soon find a furnace; he who has flour can soon find an oven, and needs to take no further care for the baking of the bread.

There is no need to write specialized books on this subject. Simply observe the <term>regulation of the fire</term> <note>original: Regiment of the Fire</note> to know how to distinguish between cold and hot. If you achieve this, you have completed the Work and brought the Art to a conclusion. For this, let the Creator of Nature be praised forever, Amen.

There are several types of <term>mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the "spirit" or volatile principle of a substance. ## A short way and Repetition, etc.

The Mercury of Metals is hot and dry, and cold and moist; it contains the four qualities <note>In traditional alchemy and medicine, the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) were the building blocks of all matter and dictated how a substance affected the body.</note>.

In Mercury lies hidden the highest <term>arcanum</term> <note>A profound secret or a powerful hidden mystery/remedy</note> for man's health, but it is not to be used raw; it must first be prepared into its essence. It is sublimed <note>A process of heating a substance until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again, used to purify it.</note> with <term>copper-water</term> <note>original: "Copper-water," likely vitriol or a solution of copper sulfate</note> and is further reduced into an oil. Volatile mercury serves for external use if a separation is made by some means and it is brought into a subtle, clear liquor and then to a reddish-brown powder; once its acquired corrosiveness is removed, it may then be suitable for other uses.

The mixed Mercury serves for internal use.

Once the Mercury is purified, it is precipitated with the <term>blood of Venus</term> <note>In alchemy, Venus represents copper; "blood of Venus" refers to a red substance derived from copper</note> and is well-digested with distilled vinegar; in this way, its corrosive quality is removed. ### Of Antimony.

It is very difficult for craftsmen <note>original: Mechanicks</note> to finish learning with their tools <note>original: compasses</note>, because that great *Architect* JEHOVAH has reserved many things for His own power. We find **Antimony** in the same condition; it is very difficult to find out all the mysteries that are hidden within it. Its virtue <note>inherent power or efficacy</note> is miraculous, its power is great, and the color hidden within it is varied. Its crude body is poisonous, yet its essence is an antidote against poison. It is like **Quick-silver**, which ignorant *Physicians* can neither comprehend nor find; but the knowledgeable **Physician** believes it to be true, having made many experiments with it.

This Mineral contains much **Mercury**, much **Sulphur**, and little **Salt**, which is the reason why it is so brittle and easily crumbled <note>original: appliable</note>. For there is no malleability in it, by reason of the small [quantity]...

### A Short Method and Summary, etc.

Regarding the quantity of Salt, the great affinity <note>original: "amity"</note> it has for *Saturn* <note>The alchemical name for lead</note> is due to *Mercury*. For "Philosophers' Lead" is made from it, and it is attracted to Gold because of its Sulphur; it purifies Gold, leaving no impurity in it. There is an operation in it equal to that of Gold, if it is well prepared and administered to a person medicinally. It flies out of the fire <note>it is volatile</note> and yet remains firmly in the fire <note>it is fixed</note>, if it is prepared accordingly. Its volatile spirit is poisonous and purges the body severely, not without causing damage. However, its remaining fixed part also purges, but not in the same manner as the volatile spirit; it does not provoke bowel movements <note>original: "stool"</note> but instead seeks out the disease wherever it is, penetrating the entire body and all its members. It allows no evil to remain there, expels it, and restores the body to a better condition.

In brief, *Antimony* is the "Lord of Medicines." A <term>Regulus</term> <note>The metallic form of a mineral after it has been separated from its ore</note> is made from it using Tartar and Salt. If some iron filings are added during the melting of *Antimony* using a specific manual technique, a wonderful Star comes forth, which Philosophers <note>The original text omits the 'o'</note> before me called the *Signat-star* <note>A star-like crystalline pattern that forms on the surface of purified antimony, considered a sign of high purity</note>. After this Star is melted several times with cold *Earth-salt*, it becomes yellowish, possesses a fiery quality, and has wonderful efficacy. This Salt afterward produces a liquor, which is further processed into a fixed, <term>incombustible oil</term>, which serves several purposes.

Besides, curious <term>flowers</term> <note>Fine powders produced by sublimation, where a solid is heated into a vapor and then cools back into a solid powder</note>—either red, yellow, or white—are made from the common Regulus of Antimony, depending on how the fire has been managed. Extraction may also be made with vinegar and crude **antimony**, or from its *regulus* <note>original: *Regulus*; the metallic form of a mineral that settles at the bottom of a crucible during smelting</note>; however, this requires a longer time and is not as effective as the previous preparation.

**Antimony** can also be melted with cold *earth-salt* <note>likely saltpeter or another mineral salt</note>, dissolved, and digested <note>heated gently</note> for a time in spirit of wine. My conscience will not allow me to reveal all its qualities: **I** do not wish to bring the curses of **physicians** upon me. They have gone to great expense and labored much in burning **coals** for its preparation; I would not want to rob them of their livelihood. **Therefore**, learn for yourself as your predecessors did. Seek as **I** have done, and then you will also find what others have described.

An **oil** of **antimony** is also made by adding the "flying **dragon**" <note>an alchemical metaphor, often referring to a volatile substance like mercury or corrosive sublimate</note>. ### Of Copper-water.

**I**f I could prevail with Apollo <note>The Greek god of music, healing, and truth, often associated here with the inspiration for scientific discovery</note> to be merciful, and to give liberty to his Muse to assist me in describing Art and Wisdom, then I would bring an offering to Minerva <note>The Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare</note>, so the gods of wisdom might take notice of a grateful mind for the gifts they had bestowed. I would write of a mineral whose Salt is presented in the highest manner, and whose great and good qualities are of such excellence that reason is not able to comprehend or conceive of them. It was generally known by the name of **Copper-water** <note>original: "Copper-water"; likely referring to blue vitriol or copper sulfate</note>; to make its meaning and sense plain, let people know and be informed that Vitriol <note>A general term for various sulfate minerals</note> contains two spirits: a white one and a red one. The white spirit is the white Sulfur upon white; the red spirit is the red Sulfur upon red. He who has ears, let him hear!

Observe this diligently and remember every word, for they have a broad meaning; every word is as heavy as a Centner stone <note>original: "Centner stone"; a traditional unit of weight, usually about 100 pounds, implying the "weighty" importance of the words</note>. The white spirit is sour, creates an appetite, and causes good digestion in a person's stomach. The red spirit is even sourer and is heavier than the white; in its distillation, a fire must be continued longer because it is more "fixed" <note>original: "fixer"; meaning stable under heat and less volatile</note> in its degree. From the white spirit, by distilling the Sulfur of Lune <note>original: "Lune"; the alchemical name for silver</note>, "potable silver" <note>original: "argentum potabile"; a liquid preparation of silver used in medicine</note> is made. In the same manner, gold—being broken down in the spirit of common salt <note>likely hydrochloric acid</note> and made "spiritual" through distillation, and its sulfur removed and joined with a red spirit in a proper dose so that it may be dissolved—is then for a time putrefied <note>allowed to decay or ferment in a sealed vessel</note> in spirit of wine <note>ethanol or concentrated alcohol</note> to be further digested and often abstracted <note>distilled or drawn off</note>,

There is also a vitriol made of iron, which has a strange quality. For iron and copper are very closely related and belong together, like a husband and wife. This secret should have been kept hidden, but because it is of such great importance, I could not help but speak of it.

When vitriol is corroded with sal-ammoniac <note>term: sal-ammoniac; ammonium chloride, often used as a solvent or flux in alchemical experiments</note>, a combustible sulfur arises during its sublimation <note>term: sublimation; the process of heating a substance so it turns into vapor and then solidifies again, used for purification</note>, along with its mercury. There is very little mercury, however, because the substance is mostly made of sulfur. If this same sulfur is released again by the "Eagle" <note>term: the Eagle; an alchemical term often referring to sal-ammoniac or a specific mercurial solvent used to "open" metals</note> using spirit of wine <note>term: spirit of wine; highly distilled alcohol or ethanol</note>, a medicine can be made from it, as I have told you before. 

Although there is a more direct way to make a combustible sulfur from vitriol—such as by precipitating it after it has been dissolved by the salt or liquor of tartar <note>term: liquor of tartar; a solution of potassium carbonate</note>, or by a common lye <note>original: lixivium</note> made of beech-ashes—this first method is still the best. This is because the "body" of the vitriol is more effectively opened and prepared by the "Key of the Eagle." 

There are other secrets hidden in vitriol that are excellent in their practical application. This is clearly known, as *Venus* <note>original: Venus; the alchemical name for copper</note> and *Mars* <note>original: Mars; the alchemical name for iron</note> bear witness through their spirits, as do *Sol* <note>original: Sol; gold</note> and *Lune* <note>original: Lune; silver</note>. But I do not intend to write a complete book on *surgery* <note>original: Chirurgery</note> at this time, nor to list every specific detail in praise of vitriol. I have already written quite enough about it; you must learn and search for yourselves. You will find that vitriol needs no advocate <note>original: Proctor</note> to speak on its behalf. Its very nature will provide you with a complete medical manual, containing a third of the "universal" knowledge needed to fight all kinds of diseases.

This is the reason why, through its superabundant <term>calidity</term> <note>original: "calidity"; meaning heat or warmth</note>, it heats other things, digests them, and finally brings them to full maturity, provided the fire is continued for a certain time.

By this, nature enabled me to become a soothsayer—by the permission of the Highest Creator—so that this nobly implanted quality might be confirmed by the faithful and true evidence of one of her devoted disciples.

### A Short Method and Repetition, etc.

An oil can be made from it by itself (*per se* <note>original: *per se*; meaning "on its own" or "without additives"</note>), which is effective against putrid, stinking wounds. It destroys and kills any worms that grow in them, especially if the small amount of salt within it is dissolved from its sulfur.

A balsam is made from it using salad oil <note>original: "Sallet Oyl"; likely olive oil</note> or oil of juniper, or similarly with white spirit of turpentine. It has a red color and is prepared as follows: take flowers of sulfur <note>a powdered form of sulfur produced by sublimation</note> made with the colcothar <note>original: "Colcotar"; the brownish-red residue, mostly iron oxide, left after the distillation of vitriol</note> of vitriol <note>sulfuric acid or a sulfate mineral</note>. Digest <note>the process of steady, gentle heating</note> them for a time in horse dung <note>used in alchemy as a source of consistent, low-level heat</note> or by any other method. This balsam may be safely used for those suffering from a consumption of the lungs <note>tuberculosis</note>, especially if it is rectified <note>purified by repeated distillation</note> several times with spirit of wine <note>ethanol or concentrated alcohol</note>, distilled, and separated until it is blood-red. This balsam serves as a preservative against corruption and decay.

The quintessence <note>the purest or most concentrated essence of a substance</note> of sulfur is found in a mineral where a sulfurous flint is formed. These crushed pebbles are placed in a glass vessel, and a strong *aqua fortis* <note>original: "Aquafort"; literally "strong water," referring to nitric acid</note>, made of vitriol and saltpeter <note>potassium nitrate</note>, is poured over them. Let whatever can be dissolved dissolve, then remove the liquid. The remainder must be thoroughly dulcified <note>washed to remove acidity or salts</note> and reverberated <note>heated in a furnace where the flames are reflected back onto the material</note> until it turns red. Pour spirit of wine onto that and extract its tincture <note>a medicinal solution in alcohol</note>. Afterward, circulate <note>a process of continuous distillation and condensation</note> it for a time in a pelican <note>a specialized alchemical vessel with two side-arms for returning condensed liquid to the body</note>. Allow all the essence of sulfur to be separated; it will remain below the spirit of wine, appearing like thick salad oil because of its weight. A dose of six grains <note>a very small unit of weight, roughly 390 milligrams</note> is found to be sufficient. If you digest myrrh, aloes, and other spices in this essence of sulfur, it extracts their virtues <note>medicinal properties</note> and turns them into a balsam. This balsam prevents flesh or any other parts prone to putrefaction from decaying. For this reason, the ancients gave it this name: *Balsamus mortuorum* <note>original: *Balsamus mortuorum*; Latin for "Balsam of the Dead," used for embalming or preserving tissue</note>.

## Of Sal-ammoniac.

**Sal-ammoniac** <term>ammonium chloride</term> is one of the most important keys for opening metals. Consequently, the ancients compared it to a volatile bird. It must be prepared; otherwise, you cannot achieve anything with it. For if it is not prepared, it does more harm than good to metals, carrying them away through the chimney. With its swift wings, it can elevate and sublime <note>original: "sublime"; the process of heating a substance into vapor that then deposits as a solid</note> the tincture <note>original: "tincture"; the essential essence or spirit</note> of minerals and of some metals to the very mountain tops where snow is found—even during the greatest heat of the summer. If it is sublimed with common salt, it then purges and clears the substances and may be used safely.

Anyone who thinks they can transmute metals using only this salt—which is so volatile—certainly fails to hit the nail on the head, for the salt possesses no such power. However, it has sufficient power to break down metals and make them ready for transmutation; for no metal can be transmuted unless it is first prepared for that process. 

The greater strength within me may be drawn out through subliming and cementing <note>original: "cementing"; a process of heating a metal surrounded by reactive powder to change its properties</note>. You will find my greatest secret when I am united with the Hydra <note>an alchemical allegory, likely referring to a powerful acidic solvent or mercury</note>, which is to devour and swallow me so that I may also turn into a water serpent with her. Then I have prepared a bath for the Nymph <note>often representing a stage of purification or a specific liquid state in the chemical process</note> and have gained the power to prepare a crown for the King <note>the King typically represents Gold or the perfected Philosopher's Stone</note>, so that it may be adorned with jewels and set upon his head with honor and glory.

## Of Tartar.

**T**his salt is not listed in the book of minerals, but is generated from a vegetable seed. However, its Creator has put such power <note>original: "vertue"</note> into it that it bears a wonderful love and friendship toward metals, making them malleable. It purges <term>Lune</term> <note>Silver</note> to a brilliant whiteness and incorporates into it such additives as are suitable for it. When it is digested for a time with minerals or metals, and then sublimated and reduced <note>original: "vilified"; in this context, it likely refers to breaking the substance down to its base components</note>, they all turn into a liquid <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "quick Mercury"</note>. There is no other vegetable salt besides this one that can do this—is this not a wonderful thing! The orator is yet to be born who possesses the ability and eloquence to sufficiently express all the mysteries hidden within it.

However, making the <term>Philosophers stone</term> out of it is not possible; because it is a vegetable substance, that specific power is not granted to any of the vegetables. In <term>Medicine</term> <note>original: "Medicina"</note> it is a very good remedy, to be used both internally and externally. When its salt is made "spiritual" and sweet <note>refined through alchemical processes such as distillation to remove impurities and harshness</note>, it dissolves and breaks the stone in the bladder, and it dissolves the coagulated <term>tartar</term> of <term>gout</term> <note>Early modern physicians believed gout was caused by mineral-like "tartar" deposits in the joints</note> settled in the joints or anywhere else. Its ordinary spirit, which is used for "opening" metals <note>making metals chemically reactive or breaking their solid form</note>, when applied externally, also lays a foundation for healing those ulcers that are very difficult to cure, such as <term>fistulas</term>, <term>cancers</term>, <term>wolves</term> <note>original: "Wolves"; a historical term for "lupus" or any corrosive skin ulcer that "devoured" the flesh</note>, and similar ailments. I know nothing more to write regarding tartar, as it has separated itself and left its noblest part behind in the wine.

### Of Vinegar.

**In** **Alchemy** and **Medicine**, almost nothing can be prepared without vinegar setting a helping hand to it. Therefore, I thought it appropriate to give it its due praise and commendation, especially by including it here in this treatise. In alchemy, it is used to bring metals and minerals into **putrefaction** <note>original: "putrifaction"; the process of breaking down a substance through decay or fermentation to release its inner essence</note>. It is also used to extract their essences and tinctures once they have been prepared for it, just as the **spirit of wine** <note>alcohol or ethanol</note> is commonly used to extract tinctures from vegetables.

In medicine <note>original: "Physick"</note>, it also deserves praise, for it separates the pure from the impure and is a **separator**. It removes the sharpness and corrosiveness from mineral medicines and **fixes** <note>stabilizes a volatile substance so it no longer evaporates or changes easily</note> that which is volatile. It is also a great defense against poison, as I told you when I spoke of **antimonial glass** <note>a glass-like substance made from antimony, used in early chemistry to induce vomiting or as a chemical base</note>.

Vinegar is used internally as well, and both humans and animals are benefited by it. Externally, it is applied to hot inflammations and swellings as a cooling agent. Spirit of wine and vinegar are of great use in both alchemy and medicine; both are derived from wine and are of the same substance, but they differ in quality because of the fermentation <note>original: "putrifaction"</note> the vinegar underwent, which I mentioned to you previously.

I must acquaint you with one thing, which is this: that this is not the **Philosophers' Vinegar**. Our vinegar, or *acetum* <note>Latin: vinegar</note>, is another liquid—namely, a specific matter itself. For the **Philosopher's Stone** is made out of the **Azoth** <note>original: "Azot"; in alchemy, the "universal solvent" or the essential transformative agent</note> of the Philosophers. This must be prepared with ordinary distilled Azoth, with spirit of wine, and with other waters besides, and it must be reduced to a certain order.

Take note of this as a memorandum: if distilled pure vinegar is poured upon destroyed Saturn <note>original: "deſtroyed Saturn"; Saturn is the alchemical name for lead. "Destroyed" refers to lead that has been chemically altered, likely into lead oxide or lead acetate.</note> and is kept warm in a Marie’s-bath <note>original: "Marie's-bath"; a *bain-marie* or water bath used for gentle, indirect heating.</note>, it loses its acidity altogether and becomes as sweet as any sugar. Then, distill off <note>original: "abſtract"</note> two or three parts of that vinegar and set it in a cellar; you will then find white transparent stones, like crystals. These are an excellent cooler and healer of all adust <note>original: "aduſt"; an archaic medical term meaning dried out, parched, or inflamed due to internal heat.</note> and inflamed symptoms. If these crystals are reduced into a red oil and poured upon Mercury that has been precipitated by Venus <note>original: "Mercury, precipitated by Venus"; Mercury chemically reacted with copper (Venus).</note>, and you proceed further as you should—if that is done correctly—then neither Sol nor Luna <note>original: "Sol nor Lune"; the Sun and Moon, alchemical symbols for gold and silver.</note> will hinder you from obtaining riches.

### *Of Wine.*

The true vegetable stone <note>The "vegetable stone" refers to a substance derived from plants—specifically wine—believed by alchemists to hold medicinal or transformative powers similar to the Philosopher’s Stone.</note> is found in Wine, which is the noblest of all plants. It contains three sorts of Salt, three sorts of Mercury, and three sorts of Sulphur.

The first Salt resides in the wood of the vine. If the wood is burnt to ashes and a lixivium <note>original: "lixivium"; a liquid solution made by leaching wood ashes, commonly known as lye.</note> is made from it, its salt can be drawn forth, which must then be coagulated. This is the first Salt.

The second Salt is found in Tartar <note>original: "Tartar"; the potassium bitartrate crystals that naturally deposit in wine barrels during fermentation.</note>. If that is incinerated, you may draw its salt forth; dissolve and coagulate it several times until it is sufficiently clarified.

The third Salt is this: when the Wine is distilled, it leaves dregs <note>original: "feces"</note> behind. These are turned into powder, and their salt can be drawn out with warm water. Each of these Salts has a special property, yet in their center they exist in harmony because they descend from one root.

For two guilders <note>original: "Gilders"; a gold or silver coin used in Europe</note> you may buy this material for the work. Let it crystallize <note>original: "shoot"</note> into the vitriol <note>original: "Vitriol"; a sulfate of a metal, used here as a key alchemical starting point</note>, which must be "sweet," without any corrosiveness or the sharpness of salt. # SECTION III.

## Of the Philosophers' Magnet.

**H**ermes, the father of Philosophers, possessed this Art and was the first to write about it. He prepared the stone out of the *Mercury*, *Sun* (*Sol*), and *Moon* (*Luna*) <note>original: *Sol* and *Luna*; alchemical terms for gold and silver</note> of the Philosophers. Many thousands of practitioners have imitated him, and I have done the same myself. I speak truly when I say that the Philosophers' Stone is composed of two bodies; its beginning and ending must be with *Philosophical Mercury*.

And this is now the *first matter* <note>original: *prima materia*</note>, otherwise known as the *prey* <note>original: *preda*</note>. The *first matter* <note>the fundamental, unformed substance from which all things are made</note> belongs only to God, and it is solidified in the bowels of the Earth—first into *Mercury*, then into *Lead*, then into *Tin* and *Copper*, then into *Iron*, and so on. Therefore, the solidified *Mercury* must, through Art, be turned back into its *first matter* or water—that is, *Mercurial water*. This is a "stone and yet no stone," from which is made a volatile fire in the form of a water, which drowns and dissolves its fixed father and its volatile mother <note>In alchemy, the "fixed father" often represents sulfur/gold, while the "volatile mother" represents mercury/silver</note>.

*Metallic Salt* is an imperfect body which turns into *Philosophical Mercury* <note>The original text reads "Mercy," likely an OCR error for "Mercury"</note>—that is, into a permanent or blessed water. It is the *Philosophers' Magnet*, which loves its *Philosophical Mars* <note>associated with iron</note>, sticks to him, and remains with him. Thus, our *Sun* (*Sol*) has a *Magnet* as well, and this *Magnet* is the first root and matter of our stone. If you conceive of and understand what I am saying, then you are the richest person in the world.

Hermes says that three things are required for the work: first, a volatile or *Mercurial water*—the *celestial water* <note>original: *aqua cælestis*</note>...

## CHAPTER II.

### Of the Sulfur of Tin.

**1.** A salt is made from <term>Tin</term><note>original: Jupiter</note> just like the one made from <term>Lead</term><note>original: Saturn</note>. From this, a red, sweet oil is extracted and distilled. This oil tints lead—after the lead has first been <term>calcined</term><note>burned to a powder</note> with <term>sal ammoniac</term><note>ammonium chloride</note>—into gold.

### CHAP. III.

#### Of Sulphurs of Mars and Venus.

1. **T**ake several pounds of verdigris <note>A green pigment/crust formed on copper; copper acetate</note> and extract its tincture with distilled vinegar. Let it crystallize, and you will have a glorious vitriol, from which you may distill a red oil using a retort <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note>. This oil dissolves Mars <note>Iron</note>, turning it into a vitriol, which is reduced over a long time in a great fire into a red oil. Then you will have the combined sulfur of Mars <note>Iron</note> and Venus <note>Copper</note>. Add some sulfur of gold, coagulate it, and fix <note>To make a volatile substance solid or stable when heated</note> it. You will then have a medicine which improves <note>original: "meliorateth"</note> both men and metals.

2. Silver is refined <note>original: "graduated"</note> with this oil, and a good portion of the "King's Crown" <note>An alchemical term for high-purity gold</note> is obtained.

3. Take two equal parts of gold and silver beaten into thin plates <note>original: "laminated"</note> and melt them together. If they are putrefied in this oil for a day and a night, it turns them into good gold. In this oil, you will find many strange effects and virtues. Praise be to God <note>original: "Laus Deo"</note>.

## Chapter IV.

### Of Sulfur of Gold

1. **I** have previously described how gold is made "spiritual" to create the "Purple Mantle" <note>original: "Purple Mantle"; this likely refers to a specific alchemical preparation of gold, often associated with a deep red or purple color indicative of high purity or the Philosopher's Stone</note>. Now, if you intend to make *aurum potabile* <note>original: "aurum potabile"; Latin for "potable gold," a medicinal liquid gold thought to have curative powers</note>, you may dissolve that spiritual gold with oil of vitriol <term>sulfuric acid</term>, extract it, and distill it with spirit of wine <term>ethanol or concentrated alcohol</term>. This is a medicine that cures many difficult diseases and has wonderful effectiveness.

2. This *solar sulfur* <note>The essential "soul" or active principle of gold</note> transforms prepared calx <term>a powdery metallic oxide</term> of *Luna* <note>Silver</note> into good gold. But as you heard in my previous writings, the King <note>Gold</note> has only an honorable garment and must collect his rents and subsidies from his subjects <note>The base metals</note>. He must be bathed in his own flourishing blood and sweat, must be destroyed and gloriously renewed; only then is he able to make his poor brothers and sisters <note>the lesser metals</note> into Kings as well, and "legitimate their bastards" <note>The author uses this metaphor to describe the process of purifying "bastard" or impure minerals into noble metals</note>.

*Antimony* is a "bastard" of *Saturn* <note>Lead</note>. However much *regulus* <note>the metallic heart or pure portion of an ore</note> it contains can be turned into *Sol* <note>Gold</note>, provided the proper dose of tincture is first added to it. *Marcasite* <note>Iron pyrites</note>, a "bastard" of *Jupiter* <note>Tin</note>, is also turned to gold by means of a tincture. *Vitriol* <note>Sulfate minerals</note> contains a metallic mercury, a "bastard" of *Venus* <note>Copper</note>; as much of it as is present can be transformed into gold.

3. If you add the solar sulfur to the sulfur of *Vitriol*, *Venus* <note>Copper</note>, and *Mars* <note>Iron</note>, and then fix <term>to stabilize a volatile substance so it can withstand heat without evaporating</term> them artificially, you will have a tincture for both people and metals that expels all kinds of diseases. This "fixed" powder specifically transforms *Luna* <note>Silver</note> into *Sol* <note>Gold</note>. *Laus Deo* <note>Latin: Praise be to God</note>.

# Of the Sulfur of Mercury.

## C H A P. V.

### Of the Sulfur of Mercury.

**M**ercury is the source of all metals and is a spiritual body and a "fugitive servant"; when it is cast into the fire, it flies into its chaos <note>original: "Chaos"; in alchemy, this refers to the formless state of matter or the air into which vapors escape during heating</note>. But he who can capture it then obtains the Sulfur of Mercury, or the Water of Sulfur, or the blessed water <note>original: *aqua benedicta*</note>, which is the Key of the Art that opens metals philosophically. The Philosophers' Mercury—not the common variety—when reduced to a liquid, dissolves the Philosophic Salt along with the "Purple Mantle" <note>original: "Purple Mantle"; a symbolic term for a specific stage or substance in the Great Work, often associated with a purple color</note> through the processes of putrefaction and distillation, for it is double mercury <note>original: *Mercurius duplicatus*</note>.

---

## C H A P. VI.

### Of the Sulfur of Luna.

1. **T**his Luna <note>original: "Lune"; the alchemical name for silver</note> is made spiritual by means of our water, the "second Key," and may easily be made into "potable silver" <note>liquid silver intended for medicinal use</note>, which cures many diseases.

2. Feed three parts of this spiritual Luna with equal parts of "Virgin's Milk" <note>original: "Virgins Milk"; a common alchemical term for a white, milky solvent or a purified mercurial water</note>, and bring two of them to fixation; you then have an increase <note>original: "augment"</note> of Luna, which "breeds monthly young ones." These are taken out, and their places are supplied with quicksilver <note>original: "Mercury vive"</note>, and so on. This powder is reduced with borax, and then you have a perpetual increase <note>original: *augmentum perpetuum*</note>.

## CHAPTER VII.

### Of the Sulfur of Antimony.

1. **T**here is a sweet extraction made out of Glass of Antimony <note>original: *Vitrum Antimonii*, a glass-like substance produced by roasting antimony ore</note> using distilled vinegar. Let the vinegar <note>original: *acetum*</note> be separated from it. Upon the remainder, pour spirit of wine <note>An early term for ethanol or high-proof alcohol</note>, which must then be extracted, and the pure substance separated from the impure. Draw this sweet extraction over and let the spirit of wine be drawn from it often by <term>cohobation</term> <note>The process of repeatedly redistilling a liquid over the same solid residue to increase its potency</note> until that powder is reduced to a glorious Oil of Antimony.

This Oil cures all manner of diseases when administered in a convenient vehicle <note>A substance, like water or wine, used to deliver a medicine</note>.

2. Further, take one part of this Oil and two parts of the <term>Mercurial water</term>, in which is dissolved a fourth part of the <term>purple Mantle</term> <note>Likely a reference to a specific alchemical precipitate or color state achieved during the work</note>. Then dissolve, join together, seal hermetically <note>original: "lute Hermetically," meaning to seal a glass vessel air-tight with clay or cement</note>, solidify, and fix. This Tincture transforms <note>original: "tingeth"</note> Silver <note>original: *Luna*</note> and Mercury into Gold <note>original: *Sol*</note>. This is that pure Sulfur of Antimony, which is made of the Glass of Antimony by itself <note>original: *per se*</note>, without any addition of saltpeter, salt, or borax.

## CHAPTER VI.
### Of Common Vitriol.

<header>Of common Magnet.</header>

### S E C T I O N  I I I.

#### Of common Magnet.

1. **M**agnet contains that which common *Mars* <note>In alchemy, Mars is the symbol and name for Iron.</note> has. Common iron may easily be worked; I do not need to say many words about it. Magnet has an attractive quality to draw iron.
2. An oil is made from *Magnet* and *Mars*, which is very effective for treating deep wounds.
3. With magnet and antimony, "fixed silver" <note>original: *Lune fix*; silver that has been chemically treated to resist certain tests or to be more stable.</note> is made; this is graduated <note>Refined or "raised" in grade and quality toward the state of gold.</note> and made into gold with the oil of *Mars* and *Venus* <note>In alchemy, Venus is the symbol and name for Copper.</note>. This may also be accomplished with antimony and *Mars*.

Thus I finished my course and discovered many things during my work. My fellow brethren became alchemists, and all possessed the philosopher's stone. I was the first to begin and took great pains before I attained anything. If you read my writings diligently, you will find the *prima materia* <note>original: "first matter"; the primordial base substance required for the alchemical "Great Work."</note>, or philosopher's mercury, along with the philosophical salt, in the *Parable of the XII Keys* <note>A reference to "The Twelve Keys of Basil Valentine," a famous 15th-century alchemical text.</note>. I have expressly described the philosophical sulphur, or ferment.

Now I conclude and commit you to God, and I ask you to remember me.

->*The blessed hold to the middle way.* <note>original: "Medium Tenuere Beati."</note><-

<header>A Process upon the Philosophical [Work]</header>

# Jod. V. R.

## A Process upon the Philosophical work of Vitriol.

Having obtained this process in the aforementioned year, and afterward—as you shall hear—having worked and elaborated it with my own hands without anyone supervising me, I was heartily rejoiced, as if I had been born again, and returned sincere thanks to God. I did not plainly describe its practice at first because I had erred in its composition and was obliged <note>original: "fain"</note> to begin the work anew. 

Having failed in my work, I began again in the year 1605. Because the "matter of the Earth" and the <term>spirit of Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, the "spirit of Mercury" refers to the volatile, transformative principle extracted from a substance.</note> were not sufficiently purified, the earth could not be perfectly united with the water during the composition. I set that attempt aside entirely and began a new process at the end of the year 1605 in the City of Strasbourg. I used more diligence and exactness, and then my work (God be praised) prospered better, for which I am still thankful to God. 

In the name of the Holy Trinity, on the 19th of October, 1605, I took ten pounds of <term>Vitriol</term> <note>Vitriol: A historical term for metal sulfates, likely iron (green vitriol) or copper (blue vitriol) in this context.</note> and dissolved it in warmed, distilled rain-water. I let it stand for a day and a night, at which time much sediment <note>original: "feces"</note> had settled. I filtered the matter and evaporated it gently, <term>until a skin formed</term> <note>original: "ad cuticulam usque"; an alchemical term for evaporating a liquid until a thin film appears on the surface, signifying it is ready to crystallize.</note>. 

I placed it in a cool spot to crystallize. This crystallized vitriol I <term>calcined</term> <note>original: "calcicated"; to heat a substance to high temperatures to drive off volatile parts or reduce it to a powder.</note> and dissolved it again in distilled rain-water. I let it crystallize again, repeating this work until the vitriol achieved a celestial green color.

Having no more any dregs <note>original: "feces"</note> about it, it lost all its corrosiveness and was of a very pleasant taste.

This highly putrefied vitriol <note>original: "Vitriol"; likely iron(II) sulfate, often called green vitriol</note>, in its raw state and not yet calcined <note>original: "calcined"; heated to a high temperature to drive off volatile matter</note>, I placed into a coated retort <note>a glass vessel with a long downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note>. I distilled it over an open fire, driving it over for twelve hours under a carefully controlled fire in a white fume. When these fumes ceased and the red corrosive oil began to appear, I extinguished the fire. 

The next morning, once everything was cold, I removed the receiver <note>the vessel that collects the distillate</note> and poured the contents of the receiver into a flask <note>original: "body"</note>. Since some of the lute <note>sealing clay or cement used to join the glassware</note> had fallen into it, I filtered it and obtained a clear solvent <note>original: "menstrual water"; in alchemy, a "menstruum" is a solvent capable of extracting essences</note>. This contained some phlegm <note>original: "phlegme"; a watery, inactive distillate</note> because I used uncalcined vitriol. I then drew off the liquid in a water bath <note>original: "Balneo" or "Bain-marie"</note> until not a single drop of water remained in it.

I found my "Chaos" <note>the raw, disorganized matter at the center of the alchemical process</note> at the bottom, which was a dark red and very heavy. I poured this into a vial, sealed it hermetically <note>original: "Hermeticè"; airtight seal</note>, and placed it on a tripod inside a wooden globe within a steam bath. I left it there until it was entirely dissolved. After several weeks, it separated into two parts: a bright, transparent water and an "earth," which settled to the bottom of the glass in the form of a thick, black, corrosive substance resembling pitch. 

I separated the "white spirit" from it and returned the fluid black matter to be dissolved again. I once more separated the white spirit that was produced from it. I repeated this work until nothing remained at the bottom except a dry red earth. After that, I purified my white spirit through distillation <note>original: "per distillationem"</note> very precisely; it was as pure as a tear that falls from the eye. I dried <note>original: "exiccated"</note> the remaining earth under a muffle furnace <note>original: "Muffle"; a furnace in which the subject is heated without direct contact with the fuel</note> until it was as porous and dry as dust. Over this, I again poured my white spirit and set it to digest <note>original: "digestion"; a process of slow, gentle heating to encourage chemical change</note>. This spirit extracted the sulfur <note>original: "Sulphur"</note>, or "Philosophical Gold."

Sublime this mercury by degrees of fire <note>original: *per gradus ignis*</note>. In the first place, I will inform you what that true and highest *aurum potabile* <note>original: *aurum potabile*; literally "drinkable gold," a legendary alchemical medicine thought to be a universal panacea</note> and Universal Medicine is. ### Of the Microcosm <note>original: Microcosme</note>.

In the first place, we must consider the matter and form of this world. This matter was shaped out of a formless state—or a "nothing"—and the great Creator immediately prescribed an order for this matter, establishing how it should be governed as soon as it came to life or motion. In closing, I wish for everyone the grace and blessing of God, the Creator of all creatures, so that they may be blessed, wise, and rich, both in this temporal and corruptible world, and in the next world attain eternal bliss.

->*Amen.*<-

->Particulars from the seven metals, how they<-

->*First, concerning the Sulphur of Gold <note>original: "Sol"</note>, by which Silver <note>original: "Lune"</note> is*<-

Take pure gold that has been cast three times through antimony <note>a process used to purify gold by removing base metals</note>, and six parts of well-purified quicksilver <note>original: "Mercury vive"</note> which has been pressed through leather. Create an amalgam <note>a soft alloy of mercury and another metal</note> from these. To the amount of this amalgam, grind <note>original: "rind"</note> twice as much common sulfur. Let it evaporate in a broad pan over gentle heat under a muffle <note>a furnace chamber that protects the material from direct contact with the flame</note>, stirring it constantly with an iron hook. Therefore, because of his Soul, Man is considered a fixed creature. # Of the Great Stone

Take a piece of the finest gold and separate it into its parts by the means that Nature has granted to the lovers of **Art** <note>original: "Art"; here referring to the practice of alchemy</note>, just as an anatomist dissects a human corpse to examine the internal organs. That is, they were made from a penetrating, subtle spirit, a pure and immaculate soul, and an astral salt and balsam. 

Once joined, these elements are nothing but a **Mercurial Liquor** <note>original: "Mercurial Liquor"; a liquid form of mercury considered the "living water" or "universal solvent" in alchemy</note>. This water was brought to school to its own god, *Mercury*, who examined the water. Finding it to be legitimate and without deceit, he befriended it and joined with it in matrimony. From both of them, an incombustible oil was created. Then *Mercury* grew so proud that he hardly recognized himself; he cast off his eagle's wings <note>The "wings" represent volatility; casting them off suggests the mercury has become "fixed" or stable</note> and swallowed the slippery tail of the **dragon** <note>The "Dragon" often represents raw, chaotic matter or corrosive acids used in the process</note>, then offered battle to *Mars*.

Then *Mars* gathered his champions together and commanded that *Mercury* should be imprisoned. *Vulcan* <note>The god of fire, representing the heat of the alchemist's furnace</note> was appointed as his **jailer** until he could be freed by someone of the female kind.

After rumors of these events spread, the other planets met and held a council. They considered what should be done so that they might proceed wisely. Then *Saturn*, the first in order, began to speak with a fierce **speech** in this manner:

The king’s crown <note>original: "Diadem"</note> is made of pure gold, and a chaste bride must be married to him.

**By** water, fire may be wholly extinguished; if much water is cast into a little fire, then the fire gives way to the water and yields the victory to it. In the same way, our fiery Sulphur <note>original: "Sulphur"; in alchemy, this represents the soul, the combustible principle, or the "active" masculine force of a substance.</note> must be conquered and overcome by water prepared according to the Art <note>original: "Art"; referring to the "Great Work" or the practice of alchemy.</note>.

He must give it the Key of his own proper color, so that he may be destroyed and made invisible by it. A painter <note>original: "Limner"</note> can paint yellow upon white, and red upon yellow, and then a purple color; and although all the colors appear, the last one greatly excels in its degree. The same ought to be observed in our *Magistery* <note>original: "Magistery"; the mastery of the alchemical process or the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. Once this is done, you will have before your eyes the light of all wisdom, which shines in darkness but does not burn.

For our Sulphur does not burn, yet it shines far and near. Neither does it dye <note>original: "tinge"; to chemically transform or change the color of a metal.</note> anything unless it is prepared and imbued with its own tincture <note>original: "tincture"; the active medicinal or transformative essence of the alchemical stone.</note>, by which it may afterwards transform weak and imperfect metals. For the weaker cannot overcome, but the stronger may obtain the victory over the weaker, and the weak must yield to the strong. Therefore, observe the following conclusion for this discourse:

That which is weak cannot help the weak.

### The XII Keys.

The life-giving <note>original: "vivifying"</note> power of the Earth produces everything that proceeds from it. Anyone who says that the Earth is without life is in error.

For that which is dead cannot add to that which has life, and the offspring of the dead cease to exist because the Spirit of Life is missing. Therefore, the Spirit is the Life and Soul of the Earth; it dwells within it and acts upon earthly things through celestial and astral <note>original: "Syderial," referring to the influence of the stars</note> influences. All herbs, trees, and roots—as well as all metals and minerals—receive their power, growth, and nourishment from the Spirit of the Earth. This Spirit is Life itself, which is nourished by the stars and provides sustenance to all plant life <note>original: "Vegetables," used here in the archaic sense of all growing flora</note>. Just as a mother protects the *fetus* <note>original: "Fetus"</note> in the womb and feeds it there, so the Earth nourishes minerals in its bosom through the Spirit it receives from above.

Therefore, the Earth does not provide these virtues by itself, but through the living Spirit within it. If the Earth were without that Spirit, it would be dead and could no longer yield any nourishment. This is because the Spirit would lack that sulphur or "fatness" <note>original: "Fatness," an alchemical term for the oily, combustible principle that allows for growth and vitality</note> which preserves life-giving power and produces all growing things through its sustenance.

Two opposing spirits may dwell together, but they do not easily agree. For when gunpowder is lit, those two spirits of which it is made flee from one another with great noise and violence. They vanish into smoke, so that no one knows where they have gone or what they were, unless they knew by experience which spirits they were and in what substance <note>original: "subject"</note> they had their being.

### The XII Keys

...pleasant voice of the Queen, and out of his great love, he embraces her and satisfies himself with her until both vanish and become one body.

It is commonly said that two men can overcome and conquer one, especially if there is enough space to exercise their fury. Therefore, know from a true foundation that a double wind called *Vulturnus* <note>The Roman name for the East-Southeast wind</note> must come, and then a single wind called *Notus* <note>The South wind</note>. These will blow fiercely from the East and South; but when they cease, so that water is made from the air, then be confident that a physical <note>original: "Corporeal"</note> thing may be made from a spiritual one. The number will hold power through the four parts of the year in the fourth heaven <note>In ancient cosmology, the fourth heaven is the sphere of the Sun</note>, after the seven planets <note>In alchemy, the seven planets represent the seven metals: Gold, Silver, Mercury, Copper, Iron, Tin, and Lead</note> have exercised their dominion. **A**ll flesh, whether it belongs to humans or beasts, yields no increase or propagation unless it is first putrefied <term>putrefied: decomposed or decayed; in alchemy, this is the essential stage of "death" that must precede the "rebirth" of a substance</term>. # The XII Keys

Many insects and worms receive life so that by mere putrefaction <note>original: "putrifaction"; the process of decay or rotting, which alchemists believed was the essential first step for transformation and new life.</note> they attain a life-giving <note>original: "vivifying"</note> power and movement. This should be rightly esteemed as a wonder above all wonders. Nature has granted this, for the same life-giving increase and inspiration of life is found abundantly in the Earth; for the same reason, it is excited in its spiritual seed by the other elements <note>The four traditional elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note>.

This is demonstrable by examples. The country housewife knows it very well, for she cannot produce a hen for her use except through the decay <note>The author views the breakdown of the egg's contents during incubation as a form of "putrefaction" necessary for the generation of the chick.</note> of the egg, out of which the chicken is generated.

If bread falls into honey, ants are bred there, which is also a unique mystery in Nature above others. The countryman also understands that worms emerge from the rotting flesh of men, horses, and other beasts, as well as spiders and worms in nuts, apples, and pears. No one is able to list the various kinds and species of worms that arise from putrefaction <note>The author is describing "spontaneous generation," a widely held belief until the 19th century that living organisms could arise directly from decaying matter.</note>.

The same is also observed in vegetables; various kinds of herbs, such as nettles and many others, grow in places where they never grew before and where no seed fell, arising only through putrefaction. The cause is that the earth in those places is predisposed and, as it were, impregnated for those productions. This has been infused from above by a sidereal <note>original: "syderial"; relating to the stars or constellations and their perceived influence on earthly matter.</note> property, so that the seed has been spiritually formed within them. This seed decays within the Earth, and by the operation and assistance of the elements, it generates a physical <note>original: "corporeal"</note> matter according to its natural species. First, by continual heat turned into vinegar, its spirit is not as volatile as before; for in the distillation of the vinegar, its water or phlegm comes first, and the spirit last. World, where he shall feel everything that he could not comprehend in his silent capacity. If anyone should intend to teach me any other way with a long-windedness of words, he may fill me with words, but he must also prove it in reality. For without that, I am not bound to believe his words, but rather I desire some sign—just as Thomas, one of the Twelve Apostles, who looked for <note>original: "Ocular demonstration"</note> physical proof.

<note>original: "sidereal"; relating to the stars, constellations, or celestial influences.</note>

For sidereal things are understood by sharp imagination and the rules of arithmetic, but finding out earthly things requires <term>speculation and separation</term>.
<note>In this context, "speculation" refers to deep observation or contemplation, while "separation" refers to the alchemical process of dividing a substance into its fundamental parts.</note>

With speculation, an intention must be joined, and an apprehension is attached to speculation. The former is done spiritually, because the spirit of man does not rest; it desires to grasp more qualities of the spirit in natural things. Every spirit always draws its like to itself. The rest is earthly: for an earthly body separates the physical body from the spiritual part by manual work, so that one may be discerned before and apart from the other. 

Since the soul shows herself truly in both, she is therefore truly in all things, for she ties the heavenly and earthly together like a bond. But when the heavenly is separated from the earthly, so that the soul must also forsake her body, then you have separated and received the three parts as distinct things. A hen lays an egg; that same egg is brought to a state of hardness or <term>coagulation</term> <note>original: "coagulation"; here referring to the solidifying of the egg's liquid contents through heat</note> by heat. By further heat, it is brought to a state of <term>putrefaction</term> <note>original: "putrefaction"; in alchemical philosophy, this is the essential stage where a substance breaks down so that new life can be released</note>, where it is corrupted. In this putrefaction, the egg receives a new *genus* <note>Latin: "kind" or "type"</note>, in which a new life is raised, and a chicken is hatched. Once this chicken is perfect, the shell opens, making way for the chicken to creep forth. This chicken, coming to a further ripeness and age, continues to grow according to its kind. Thus, Nature furthers her own kind and increases *unto infinity* <note>original: *Uſque ad infinitum*</note>.

It is true that the egg is not the *first matter* <note>original: *prima materia*; the fundamental, formless base substance from which all things are created</note> of the rooster or the hen; rather, the *first matter* of their flesh is the first seed from which the egg took its form. That seed, by the equal nature of the motion of both [parents], is driven together and united; from there, by further heat, it proceeded to putrefaction, and from there into a new birth, which continues to propagate and increase.

So it is with man; for one person alone cannot produce a new birth unless the seeds of both male and female are united. ## THE MANUAL
# OPERATIONS
-> OF <-
# BASIL VALENTINE,

-> By which he has prepared his medicines. <-

**I**n the name of the Eternal Trinity—God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost—I, *Basil Valentine*, <note>Basil Valentine is the pseudonym of a celebrated alchemist, traditionally identified as a 15th-century Benedictine monk, though his writings first appeared in the early 1600s.</note> do here set down those manual operations by which I have prepared my following medicines. Through God's assistance, these have made me a successful and scarcely ever-failing physician.

### *Concerning Vitriol and its Preparation, as well as its Power and Virtue.*

**T**ake good <term>Hungarian Vitriol</term> <note>original: "Hungrian Vitriol," a high-quality sulfate mineral, often copper or iron-based, prized by alchemists</note>, calcine <note>heat a substance to a high temperature but below its melting point to drive off volatile matter</note> it until it is of a yellowish color, and no darker. Grind this roasted Vitriol small, and put it into a glass distillation vessel with a long neck, properly sealed with the <term>Seal of Wisdom</term> <note>original: "luto sapientiae," a specialized airtight sealing paste used in alchemy</note>. 

Attach a large receiver vessel and begin to distill day and night with a very gentle fire, providing no more heat than the sun does on a hot day. Afterward, increase the fire by degrees, finally forcing out the spirits with the strongest fire until red, visible drops begin to pass over; this work should take three days and nights. 

When this is done, take what is left in the distillation vessel—commonly called the <term>dead head</term> <note>original: "Caput mortuum," the useless residue or dross remaining after distillation or sublimation</note>—and grind it small. Pour onto it clear, pre-distilled rainwater and boil the <term>colcothar</term> <note>original: "Cholcotar," the red iron oxide residue left after the distillation of vitriol</note> in it; the Salt of the Vitriol will then dissolve into the water. 

Once the water has settled and is clear, filter <note>original: "Filtre"</note> it so that the sediment <note>original: "Feces"</note> may be separated. Let the water evaporate <note>original: "vapour away"</note> gently in some glass vessel until the salt is dry. Dissolve the salt again in pre-distilled rainwater and let it evaporate again to dryness. Repeat this operation a third time, and the Salt of Vitriol will be very beautiful, clean, and clear. 

Put this dry salt into a <term>cucurbit</term> <note>original: "Cucurbit," a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</note> of glass, and pour the previously made spirit of vitriol over it. Seal the glass with the seal of wisdom... <note>The text ends mid-sentence; the catchword "sapientia" completes the term "luto sapientiae."</note>

### *The Use of this Medicine.*

**T**his Essence of Sulphur, when four grains of it are taken in Balm-water <note>original: "Balm-water"; likely lemon balm water, used historically for its calming and restorative properties</note>, dries up the bad humors of the blood, strengthens and incites men and women to sexual intercourse <note>original: "Copulation"</note>, cleanses the womb, prevents the <term>Rising of the Mother</term> <note>A historical medical condition also known as "hysterical passion," where various physical symptoms were attributed to the womb moving upward in the body.</note>, and produces healthy seed for the procreation of children.

The same quantity, taken in Parsley-water and continued for a fortnight <note>two weeks</note>, consumes all phlegmatic humors <note>original: "flegmatick humors"; according to the theory of the four humors, an excess of phlegm was thought to cause sluggishness and respiratory issues</note> of the entire body. It cures dropsy <note>original: "Dropfie"; a historical term for edema, or swelling caused by excess fluid</note> fundamentally, expels putrified blood, and opens abscesses <note>original: "Imposthumes"</note>. Indeed, you will find it truly performs wonderful cures if you are industrious and careful in its preparation. However, you must never, as long as you live, forget God your Creator; call upon Him for a blessing and give Him thanks for all the fatherly benefits He has bestowed upon you.

Note: This sweet Essence of Vitriol <note>Often referring to sulfuric acid or a derivative; here it is used interchangeably with the Essence of Sulphur mentioned above.</note> was taken from this book by the eminent physician Doctor Hartman and included in his *Chymical Practice* <note>original: *Praxis Chymiatrica*</note> under the title "Leprosy" <note>original: *sub titulo lepra*</note>, where he explains this process to some extent.

## *Another Medicine made out of Antimony and Mercury, and of its Effects on external Sores.*

**T**ake Hungarian antimony and sublimed mercury <term>sublimed mercury: likely mercuric chloride, a corrosive white crystalline powder</term>, and grind them well together. Distill them through an earthen retort <term>retort: a glass or ceramic vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids or gases</term>, forcing them at last with the strongest fire imaginable, and you will obtain an oil; separate this and keep it apart. Put away the quicksilver <note>original: "quick Mercury"</note>, if there happens to be any, and the cinnabar <term>cinnabar: mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral</term> you will find in the neck of the retort. 

But as for the *caput mortuum* <note>original: "Caput mortuum"; Latin for "dead head," referring to the solid residue remaining in the vessel after distillation</note>, grind it small and put it into a new retort. Having poured the oil on it (after first warming the oil), distill it from the residue again. Repeat this as many times as necessary, until the *caput mortuum* remains behind like ashes, and then your oil is prepared. 

After this, take as much fresh antimony as the first *caput mortuum* weighed, grind it small, and pour on it the oil (first warmed and distilled as many times as before) until the oil comes over as red as a ruby and the *caput mortuum* likewise remains like ashes in the bottom of the glass. Then the oil is prepared.

### *How to Make the Saltpeter Water*

## The Use.

*Note*, this Essence of Antimony has been prepared by various eminent physicians in London, who had this process communicated to them out of the High-Dutch <term>High-Dutch: the German language</term>, and it has been used with very great benefit in many desperate ailments and diseases which were considered incurable.
