### The Preparation of the Tincture of Corals.

**T**ake red coral, break it into pieces, and pour on it common hydrochloric acid <note>original: "Spirit of Salt"</note>, and the coral will be dissolved. This being done, draw off the acid by distillation and wash the remains thoroughly <term>Edulcorate: to wash away salts or impurities to sweeten or purify a substance</term>. Then, for every mark <term>Mark: a traditional European unit of weight, often equal to about 8 ounces</term> of this powder, take half an ounce of pulverized sulfur. Having mixed them together, heat them very gently <term>Reverberate: to heat a substance in a furnace or over a flame so the heat is reflected back onto it</term> until all the sulfur has burned away. Having done so, grind an equal amount of camphor with the coral and burn the camphor away in the same manner. Then wash the coral well again and pour highly rectified alcohol <note>original: "high rectified Spirit of Wine"</note> upon it. Let it digest for eight days, and the tincture of the coral will rise and infuse into the alcohol. Then pour off the liquid you have extracted and afterward distill the alcohol away from it. The tincture of coral will remain behind in the bottom, appearing like a red, fatty olive oil.

### *The Use of the Medicine.*

**S**ix drops of this tincture, given in a spoonful of wine to those who have lost their mental faculties <note>original: "bereaved of their Senses"</note>, restores them again. This tincture likewise comforts the brain, strengthens the memory, dispels sadness and melancholy <note>original: "melancholy": in this context, a clinical state of depression or a physical imbalance of the "black bile" humor</note>, makes one lighthearted, produces good blood, and strengthens the heart. It is such a noble medicine that we are indeed bound to bless Almighty God for it.

Separate the sediment from it, then likewise distill off the spirit of wine until it thickens, and set it again in a cold place so the vitriol crystallizes <note>original: "shooteth"</note> once more. 

Then put the vitriol into a glass container and draw off the phlegm <note>original: "Flegme"; the watery, inactive part of a distillate</note> by distillation in a water bath <note>original: "Balneo Mariæ"</note> until the material becomes dry. Dissolve as many pearls as possible in this vinegar, for it works very well on them, dissolving the substance but not the outer shells.

Once the pearls are dissolved, evaporate the vinegar in a water bath until the pearls are very dry. Then take them out and <term>edulcorate</term> <note>to rinse or purify a substance to remove acids or salts</note> them with rosewater. # The Manual Operations

Lastly, you must know that this medicine is a very spiritual and piercing one, which cures any illnesses <note>original: "distempers"</note> of this world in all creatures, whatever they may be. When only one grain of it is taken, it penetrates the whole body like a vapor <note>original: "fume"</note>, chases out of the body all that is bad, and replaces it with what is good. It renews the person and makes them, as it were, a new person, whom it preserves without any infirmities <note>original: "accidents"</note> throughout their life until the time ordained <note>original: "prefixed"</note> by the Most High. For against death there is no remedy. <note>original: *Contra mortem enim remedium non est.*</note>

This medicine, being first fermented with other pure gold, likewise tints <note>original: "tinge," an alchemical term for transforming the properties and color of a metal</note> many thousand parts of all other metals into very good gold, as my last Key (which is the twelfth) teaches by a specific method and process. Through this, such gold also becomes such a penetrating medicine that one part of it tints and transmutes a thousand parts of other metals—and much more, beyond belief—into perfect gold. God be blessed and praised both now and forevermore. ***Amen.***

### *Spirit of Mercury by itself, or Mercurial Water.*

**P**ut liquid mercury into a retort <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling substances</note>, and attach a receiver flask, which must be placed in a glass vessel containing water. Distill it, and the spirit will precipitate and resolve into a liquid. Pour out this liquid, and return any mercury clinging to the neck of the retort back into the vessel. Distill and rectify <note>To refine or purify a liquid through repeated distillation</note> until you have reduced the entire substance to a liquid. This Spirit of Mercury cures almost all ailments <note>original: "distempers"</note> and extracts the essence from minerals and metals.

---

### *A Tincture for both Humans and Metals.*

**T**ake the "spiritual gold" of a purple color and extract its sulfur <note>In alchemical theory, "sulfur" refers to the combustible or "soul" principle of a substance</note> using distilled vinegar. Separate the vinegar from it again so that it becomes a powder. Dissolve this powder in the Spirit of Red Mercury (which is gold), add "Salt of Gold" to it, and fix <note>To "fix" a substance in alchemy means to make a volatile or liquid substance stable and solid under heat</note> it. This is a Universal Medicine for sick and diseased human bodies, and it also serves to exalt <note>To "exalt" a metal meant to improve its purity, color, or perceived "dignity," often in the pursuit of transmutation into gold</note> metals to the highest degree.

## *A Tincture upon White* <note>A "tincture" in alchemy is a substance capable of transmuting base metals into noble ones—in this case, into silver ("white").</note>

**H**eat silver to a powder <note>original: "Calcine"</note> with salt and quicklime, and extract its blue sulfur <note>original: "blew Sulphur"; in alchemy, sulfur represents the active, combustible principle or "soul" of a metal.</note>, which you must then distill and purify with alcohol <note>original: "Spirit of Wine"</note> until it remains a liquid. I do not mean the red mercury here, but the common white mineral mercury, or rather that which is extracted out of vitriol.

Fix it then <note>original: "Fix"; to make a volatile substance solid or stable under heat.</note>, and you will have a universal medicine against all illnesses <note>original: "distempers"</note> and a tincture which transforms lead, pewter, mercury, and copper into silver.

## *To make an ounce of gold out of half an ounce*

**T**ake spirit of salt <note>original: "Spirit of Salt"; hydrochloric acid.</note> and purify it with alcohol <note>original: "Spirit of Wine"</note> until it becomes sweetish. Pour this upon the "spiritual gold" <note>likely a gold precipitate or chloride</note> of a purple color, and it will extract only the soul or sulfur of the gold, but it will not touch the "body" of the gold. The sulfur of the gold transforms silver into gold, yet in no greater quantity than the amount of gold you started with. The remaining body of the gold must then be as white as silver. Refine it upon a <term>cupel</term> <note>A shallow, porous vessel used in assaying to separate precious metals from base metals.</note> with <term>Saturn</term> <note>The alchemical name for lead.</note> and a little copper; the white body of the gold will then recover its color and properties and become good gold again.

# *To make the <term>Mercury of Gold</term>, or the <term>Philosophical Mercury</term>.*

Take the gold of a purple color, from which the <term>sulfur</term> <note>In alchemy, sulfur represented the active, combustible, and masculine principle of a substance</note> has already been extracted. Soak <note>original: "digest"</note> it with the following "water" for a month, then revitalize it by distilling it through a <term>retort</term> <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling liquids</note>. In the neck of the retort, you must lay thin iron plates. Drive the substance into a <term>receiver</term> <note>a vessel designed to collect the products of distillation</note> containing some water; it will then flow together and become a liquid <term>mercury of gold</term>.

### *The Water is made as follows.*

Take the <term>salt of urine</term> from a young man who drinks nothing but wine, and likewise <term>salt of tartar</term> <note>potassium carbonate</note> and <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note>, in equal parts <note>original: "ana," a medical term indicating equal quantities</note>. Let all of this dissolve into a liquid, which you should purify <note>original: "rectifie"</note> with <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>concentrated alcohol or ethanol</note> until it becomes very sweet. This is the <term>arcanum</term> <note>a deep secret or a powerful chemical mystery</note> through which the physical body of gold is reduced into a flowing mercury.

# *To make the <term>Salt of Gold</term>.*

Refine gold three times by pouring it through <term>antimony</term>, hammer it into thin plates, and dissolve them in *<term>aqua regia</term>* <note>original: "aqua regis," a highly corrosive mixture of acids used to dissolve gold</note>. Similarly, dissolve <term>salt of tartar</term> in <term>spirit of wine</term> and distill off the <term>phlegm</term> <note>original: "flegme," referring to the watery, tasteless distillate</note> so that what remains is like an oil. With this oil, precipitate your gold, and then separate the salt of tartar from it by washing <note>original: "ablutions"</note>. Then heat it in a furnace <note>original: "reverberate"</note> for fourteen days. Pour upon this <term>calx of gold</term> <note>the fine powder or ash left after a metal has been heated or "burnt"</note> and distill—

# Chapter 1.

## *Of things Natural and Supernatural.*

**B**ecause I intend to write about the First Tincture <note>original: "Tincture"; in alchemy, this refers to a spiritual essence or the active transformative principle of a substance.</note> and the Root of metals and minerals, and to give an account of their spiritual essence—how metals and minerals are spiritually conceived in the beginning and physically <note>original: "corporally"</note> brought forth—it is therefore necessary to state something beforehand. I wish to briefly inform you that all things are divided into the natural and the supernatural. 

Whatever is visible, tangible <note>original: "comprehensible"</note>, and has physical form is natural. But that which is incomprehensible and spiritual is supernatural, and must be understood and judged by faith. Examples of this include the Creation and, first of all, the eternity of God, which is infinite, unsearchable, and immeasurable. Nature is not capable of reaching this, nor can human reason comprehend it. This is supernatural, for it transcends reason and is understood through faith; it is therefore a divine matter and belongs to theology <note>original: "Divinity"</note>, which judges the souls of men.

Secondly, the angels of God also belong to supernatural things. They have glorified <note>original: "clarified"; meaning purified, luminous, or spiritualized</note> bodies and, by the permission of their Creator, perform deeds that no other creature is able to do, because their works are—

This is especially true of the mercy of God and his great benefits, which he shows <note>original: "sheweth"</note> to and bestows upon mankind out of his tender love—things that no one is capable of discerning or knowing completely.

### The Manual Operations

[Gold is] close, solid, and compact, because of its well-processed <note>original: "digested"</note>, ripened, and stable <note>original: "fixed"</note> body. Therefore, it can no more enter into a body than that body actually needs. But other metals do not have such a stable body; instead, their pores are open and scattered. Therefore, the coloring <note>original: "tinging"</note> Spirit can much more abundantly penetrate and inhabit them. 

However, because the bodies of these other metals are unstable <note>original: "unfixed"</note>, the Tincture <note>An alchemical substance or "medicine" capable of transforming base metals into gold or silver.</note> likewise cannot remain within these unstable bodies, but must depart from them. Since the Tincture of Gold is found more in Iron and Copper—acting as **Husband and Wife**—than in any other metal, their bodies are destroyed and the coloring Spirit is expelled from them. This creates much "blood" <note>In alchemy, "blood" often refers to the vital, life-giving essence or the red stage of the alchemical Work (the Rubedo).</note> in the opened and prepared Gold, and by feeding on this, the Gold becomes volatile <note>Capable of being evaporated or changed; the opposite of "fixed."</note>. 

Therefore, when the volatile Gold is filled by its "meat and drink," it absorbs its own blood and dries it up through its own internal fire, with the help and addition of a "moist fire" <note>Likely a reference to a water bath or gentle heat used in the laboratory.</note>. It then achieves a victory <note>original: "conquest"</note> that stabilizes <note>original: "fix"</note> it—indeed, it produces the highest level of stability. Consequently, the Gold becomes a highly stable **Medicine**, and it cannot form a physical body again because of the excessive amount of blood, unless a surplus metallic body is added to it, into which the abundant, stabilized blood can disperse itself. 

This joined metallic body is then penetrated by the exceeding heat of the stabilized blood of the **Lion** <note>In alchemical allegory, the "Lion" often represents strong mineral acids or the philosophical sulfur; here it refers to the potent, transformed Gold.</note>, acting like a fire cleansed of all impurity, and is immediately ripened to a perfect maturity and stability. ### CHAP. III.

### *Of the Spirit of Mercury.*

**A**lthough I use a unique style in my writings, which will seem very strange to many, there is a good reason for it. I believe it is enough to rely on my own experience and ignore the idle talk of others. I have gained direct knowledge of these matters, and seeing always comes before hearing; that which has a firm foundation is preferred over that which has no basis at all. Therefore, I say that all visible and tangible things are made from the Spirit of <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, the "Spirit of Mercury" (or Sophic Mercury) is not the common metal, but a universal, volatile principle or "life force" that exists within all matter.</note>, which is beyond all the earthly things of the whole world. All things are made from it and have their origin in it. Within it, everything can be found that an <term>Artist</term> <note>original: "Artist"; a term for a practitioner of alchemy or the "Hermetic arts."</note> might wish to investigate. 

It is the fundamental principle for working with metals, being a spiritual essence that is pure air. It flies back and forth without wings and is a moving wind. After it is driven out of its home by <term>Vulcan</term> <note>In alchemical symbolism, Vulcan represents the transformative power of fire and the furnace.</note>, it is forced into its <term>Chaos</term> <note>original: "Chaos"; here referring to a state of primordial, unorganized matter.</note>, which it enters again. There, it dissolves itself into the elements, where it is attracted by the stars in a magnetic way, driven by a kind of love for its origin. It seeks to be united again with its own kind because it was wrought from there originally. But when this Spirit of <term>Mercury</term> can be captured and made physical, it then resolves itself into a body and becomes a clear, beautiful, and transparent water. This is the true spiritual water, and the primary <term>Mercurial Root</term> of minerals and metals,

It is wonderful <note>original: "to be admired"</note> that the bodies of dead metals are so beautiful <note>original: "fair"</note>, whereas other dead bodies waste away to nothing. Metals also undergo decay <note>original: "corruption"</note>, but over a long period of time. Their death is like glass and retains its color, especially if it came from a *<term>Marcasite</term>* <note>In early mineralogy, "marcasite" was a general term for various crystallized metallic ores, especially iron pyrites.</note>. From this, the colors of *<term>Marcasites</term>* are learned, for green, blue, and white fluxes are found within them, just as metallic flowers are produced from three bodies.

## CHAPTER XXXVII.

### *Of Pulsa, or of the Break-stuff, or brittle matter.*

**T**his salt is usually produced by a malignant fume <note>In early mining, "fumes" often referred to toxic or sulfurous gases released from the earth.</note> which the mine-fire contains. When the stones are very hard, a wood fire must be made where the smoke draws toward the stone-fire and grows thick. If the fumes of amber <note>original: *Succinum*</note> and other substances are joined together, it turns into such a poison that the ore must be assisted, or else it is ruined. This is because a sooty cobalt <note>original: *Kobolt*; here referring to arsenic-rich cobalt ores that released toxic vapors when heated</note> fume settles on the ore, corroding and consuming it. 

To remedy this, a ball must be used. It should be round and hollow, with a hole the size of a quill. It must be so airtight that no air can enter or escape. This ball must be filled with gunpowder. Cover it with cotton-wool that has been boiled in saltpeter, then dip it in melted pitch mixed with some sulfur. Light the ball and lower it in a box, or throw it into a mine gallery <note>original: *Stolln*</note> or chamber. When the ball explodes, it expels the toxic fume—not only by its own smoke, but by the force and report <note>The "report" refers to the loud sound of the explosion.</note> the gunpowder makes. 

Such a ball may also be used in water. It can be submerged in a device under water where harmful fishes are feared; its explosion will kill the fish there. There is also a paste which makes no loud report but only burns, destroying and breaking up <note>original: "heaveth"</note> this salt. However, be careful what paste you use, and show respect to the upper scaffolds <note>The support structures within the mine shaft.</note>, whether they are old or new, so that they are not damaged or weakened <note>original: "imbezled"</note>. Your paste must be mixed so that it does no unintended harm.

# CHAPTER XXXVIII.

## Of *Clathrum*, or of the *Blank-fire*.

**T**his fire needs nothing to feed it and shines in the darkness. It is a special fire for <term>mine-works</term> that more than pays for itself if applied—returning more than the expenses spent on <term>talc</term> <note>original: "Talk"</note> or *Bromith* <note>likely an archaic term for a specific mineral or ore, possibly related to bismuth or barite</note> work. Because oil may be obtained cheaply enough in some places, this light produces no smoke and destroys harmful fumes. It is placed into a glass ball, which is then put into a basket to protect it from water and sand, providing light for the workmen. 

Miners ought to know how to enter their ground to find the height or metalline *mirror* <note>original: "Speculum." In this context, it refers to a reflective tool or a specific visual phenomenon used to detect ore</note>, which is a singular manual method. Because the metalline "breathings" <note>the vapors ancient miners believed were exhaled by metals "growing" in the earth</note> and subsequent exhalations join and come together, they require special instruments by which they may be known. Where these join and the <term>diurnal</term> <note>daily</note> breathing is predominant, it exhales by day and shines out of the earth. Miners call this a "metalline breathing." This is true, but they omit something: it is only half a breathing. If the "after-breathing" is predominant, then it appears by that *mirror* and light through which it makes itself known. Nature is at work with something, and a certain metal is at hand. Metals do shine, even though it does not appear so to our eyes, just as rotten wood <note>a reference to foxfire or bioluminescence</note> does. By day, they are not still as long as they are working, but there must be a reflection of their work, which is this light. It casts no beams as daylight or rotten wood does; by night, it receives its beam from such a dark or dusky shadowed light.

### CHAPTER 39.
#### *Of the Gluten or Mine-Glue.*

**T**he best help and remedy that may be applied to subterranean pools are wells; for where these break through, they carry that water away. However, there is no better or more immediate solution than the "Gluten" <term>Gluten: a sealing agent or "mine-glue" used to waterproof shafts and tunnels</term> to dam up or keep out the surface water <note>original: "day water"</note> so that it does not flow any further. This damming is of great utility; it not only makes the water slimy and thick, but drives it backward so that it may be directed toward another outlet, thus ridding the area of water where it is harmful <note>original: "naught"</note> and merely obstructive.

If the surface water is stopped by Gluten in this way so that it cannot flow and gather at the sink <term>sink: a drainage pit or sump at the bottom of a mine shaft</term>, then that groundwater may soon be drawn away. The more deeply the sinks are cleansed, the more these groundwaters or springs are diverted; at last, they are either turned into surface waters or dammed up and made to run another way where they will not obstruct the scaffolding <note>original: "scaffolds"; the internal timber supports of a mine</note>. In places where water-driven mills are not situated, the Gluten may be used; then the scaffolding and structures in the passages, crevices, and mines may be inspected. Dams and Gluten are the best aids for this purpose.

## CHAPTER 40.

### Concerning *Truta*, or a Paste to Corrode and Eat Through Stone.

**T**here is almost nothing that is a greater hindrance to mining operations than water. In places where the <term>gluten</term> <note>original: "Gluten"; here referring to a chemical paste or binding agent rather than the protein found in wheat</note> is not sufficient to keep water out, and where it is trapped and must be drained away with lower structures—such as with a <term>stulm</term> <note>original: "Stoln"; a horizontal tunnel or adit used to drain water from a mine</note>, or beams and pipes—it is a massive and dangerous task to make these breakthroughs effective and durable. It costs many men's lives and requires great expense. 

Therefore, ways and means must be devised to create passages through the rock using heat—specifically, to create a fire that corrodes the rock and grinds the stone, eating it until it is small and thin. This allows the water to break through and run away, so that the miners do not lose their lives in that water, as commonly happens during such works. 

This fire corrodes great stones even in running waters or rivers; it is a corrosive fire. A "gluten" or paste is made, which is then lined or covered with combustible materials and poured or cast down through a channel or pipe that is protected from the water. This ensures the paste remains effective, even if it is many fathoms deep underwater. It continues to corrode further, gathering strength from the very material it eats away at and burns, pressing steadily lower. It does not produce smoke, as it is a liquid, corrosive fire.

There are certain saps and gums which, if boiled to a hardness and mingled with unslaked lime <note>original: "unflaked lime"; quicklime, which reacts violently and generates heat when exposed to moisture</note>, kindle and burn so strongly that they corrode the rock and make a hole in it as big and as deep as

Weather also heaves a <term>stoll</term> <note>original: "stoll"; likely a mining term for a horizontal shaft (stulm) or the supportive timbering within a mine</note>, or the great beam or metallic body; why should it not also lift and heave a stone? # CHAPTER XLII.

## *Of the waste in mining operations.*
<note>original: "Of the frust in Mine-works." The word "frust" likely refers to fragments, debris, or waste rock.</note>

**T**he greatest trouble that miners face is pulling and drawing up the filth and worthless stones out of the mines so that a path can be made to go deeper. Above ground, they call this a heap of rubbish. It costs very little to cleanse, dissolve, and clear away this rubbish with corrosive water <note>original: "corrosive water"; refers to acids or chemical solutions used to break down mineral matter</note>. It costs little, if handled and managed correctly, to dissolve the lightest things first; once these are cleared away, the rest may easily be removed. 

The earth underground must not be viewed like the earth above us, which is adorned with grass; for underground, there is very little actual "earth." Instead, there is a mixture of all sorts of things, such as salts, juices <note>original: "juyces"; in alchemy, these were mineral fluids or secretions believed to nourish the growth of metals</note>, minerals, and stones. The smallest portion is actual earth, and yet that part is the most noble; for out of it, all types of metallic bodies are made. 

There are sharper substances, all of which must not be used at once; work must be performed with these when that which is above cannot be applied to that which is beneath. Mineral juices are also easy to use for corroding materials and making them brittle. Sulphur alone performs the work, acting as a poison to these juices and saps. Miners and those employed in such works must have knowledge of these things and exercise themselves through practice. Not every detail belonging to these manual tasks can be set down in black and white <note>original: "white and black"; an idiom meaning in writing or in print</note>; experimental knowledge must be joined to this, rather than depending only on written things.

# CHAPTER XLIII.

### Of the flaming fire.

Since there is a need for both large and small fires in mining operations—which must be understood and applied according to the various types of metals, and not simply based on the methods of melting and refining them—the specific conditions of these necessary fires must also be known. To record all these details would require immense effort, and writing them down would result in a massive volume. It is the responsibility of skilled melters and refiners <term>finers</term> <note>original: "Finers"</note> to manage and regulate their own fires according to the requirements of each metal's condition, so as to advance rather than hinder their work. Therefore, I leave these matters to their further and serious consideration.

---

rubs and consumes iron; therefore <term>annealing</term> <note>original: "nealing"; the process of heating and then cooling a material slowly to remove internal stresses and impurities</note> is more commendable. As they do at Mansfeld <note>a famous mining region in Germany</note>, a great heap of ore is laid together, which they kindle and let stand in a gentle, glowing heat; this burns away those impurities that should be removed during that glowing process. Metals in Sweden are treated thus by the heat of the sun in summer; there, the metal runs finely together and purifies itself so cleanly that it would be fully refined if it remained in that heat long enough. I approve of this annealing more than of <term>calcining</term> <note>original: "calcining"; heating a substance to high temperatures to change its physical or chemical constitution, usually to create a powder</note> in an open flame. There are two types of glowing fires, and metals require two types of glowing or annealing: one sort is used at Mansfeld, where they kindle heaps of shale <note>original: "slats"</note> with bundles of straw, letting them glow on their own like a heap of coals, and the ore is thus annealed. Secondly, annealing is also good for stony bodies, reducing them into <term>calxes</term> <note>original: "calxes"; the powdery metallic oxide remaining after a metal or mineral has been thoroughly heated</note>. However, those who created metallic calxes in an enclosed heat or glowing fire only obtained the calxes of the bodies' <term>exuviae</term> <note>original: "exuviums"; the discarded outer layers or waste residues of the metal</note>. Therefore, neither they nor others have any reason to wonder why they achieve no success using that method.

## CHAPTER 46.

### Of *Ignis candens*, or of the glowing fire.

**T**his fire is specifically applied to metallic <note>original: metalline</note> bodies. It consumes them, as their matter is naturally inclined toward it. This fire is of great importance, making their bodies very malleable. Their *exuviae* <note>original: exuvium's; referring to the impurities or "husks" shed during smelting</note> stay on the surface of the melt <note>original: Float</note>, and the best quality they have is that during this glowing, they shed the parts that must be removed, and the good part remains.

Nowadays, these matters are neglected. The world assumes it has enough skill and needs no further knowledge. "As many heads, so many opinions" <note>original Latin: *Quot capita tot sensus*</note>; everyone thinks their own intelligence is superior, even though some have barely begun to understand these things. This is the reason why men remain in their ignorance <note>original: rudeness</note>. People might assume that by "corrosive water" I mean *aqua fortis* <note>original: Aquafort; nitric acid</note>, but that is not the case. How many tons of precious *aqua fortis* are wasted at Goslar in the Harz Mountains <note>A historic mining district in Germany</note>? This could be put to better use, and the money spent on wood for the furnaces could have been saved.

# CHAPTER XLVII.

## Of *Ignis incubans*, or of the Lamp-fire.

<note>original: "Ignis incubans," literally "incubating fire," referring to a steady, gentle heat similar to a bird brooding over its eggs.</note>

**T**his fire serves when metals are worked openly and not <term>luted</term> <note>sealed with "lute," a clay or paste used to make vessels airtight</note> in; then the metal does not fly away as dust, nor does its best essence escape. For you have heard that a flaming fire is harmful for working with metals. <term>Lamp-dishes</term> <note>vessels heated by the flame of an oil lamp rather than coals</note> are commonly made of glass and set in an earthenware pan filled with ashes or sand, kept in a state of "sweating" <note>a gentle, moist heat used to slowly break down or transform substances</note>. In that sweat, many suppose the metal receives its body, or that one changes into the other. I leave the value of this <term>transmutation</term> <note>the alchemical process of changing base metals into noble ones</note> as it is, for I cannot approve of it. Regarding this warmth, however, I cannot disprove nor find fault with it, and all metals should indeed be dealt with in this manner.

These two fires—those of ores and the <term>Lamp-fire</term>—if they were used for medicinal purposes, would perform better than a <term>calcining</term> <note>reducing a substance to powder through high heat</note> or flaming fire can. In cases where these are of no use, a long-lasting fire must be kept steadily at a consistent heat if any good is to be accomplished. Some have kept the <term>Lamp-fire</term> in a <term>Stove-furnace</term> <note>a closed heating chamber or oven</note>, where everything was spoiled during the process; it was either too hot or too cold. It lacked a consistent heat, which the final result showed because the fire was not well-regulated.

<summary>Basilius Valentinus describes the "Lamp-fire" or incubating fire, a gentle heat used for processing metals and medicines without losing their essence. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a consistent, regulated temperature, which is often lost in improper stove-furnaces.</summary>

## CHAP. XLVIII.

### *Of the cold fire.*

**T**his is a strange fire; little can be said of it to those who cannot conceive of it. Whether it was previously overlooked, or whether earlier seekers despaired of finding it, I do not know. This is what is called "coagulating" <note>original: "coagulating"; the process of changing from a liquid to a solid or semi-solid state</note> elsewhere. It cannot consume the other type of fire; it can melt the work, but it is impossible for it to consume it. It works in the air as well as in the fire, where it demonstrates its efficacy and is the sole proof of its fusibility <note>original: "fusibleness"; the quality of being able to be melted</note>. Metallic mercury undergoes a cold fusion, whereas all other fusions are hot; if you do not believe it, feel it. The fixation of the warm flux is called coagulation; in that process, the one opposes the other. The one causes it to congeal, while the other keeps it in a liquid state. This difference must be known by those who are employed in the melting of metals and their fluxes.

It is of great importance to govern this fire well, or to know how stones are to be weighed; things that are excessively cold are death to a tempered body <note>original: "tempered body"; a body or substance in a state of balance or specific proportion</note>. As for what animals might live in either too cold or too hot a fire—to speak precisely of the nature of life is as impossible as it is to speak truly of the nature of God. Therefore, do not rely solely on definitions that human reason is able to conceive. Philosophy is strangely conditioned, and it appears by this fire also that a thing which is very cold may nonetheless contain life.

When it is in its highest degree of ascension <note>original: "ascension"; an alchemical process where a substance is vaporized or rises to the top of a vessel</note>, and then comes down again, it turns to silver, then to copper <note>catchword: copper</note>;

<summary>This chapter introduces the concept of "cold fire," or coagulation, explaining its role in the fusion and fixation of metals like mercury. The author reflects on the mysterious nature of life and the limits of human reason in defining philosophical and alchemical truths.</summary>

<keywords>cold fire, coagulation, mercury, fusion, fixation, alchemy, metals, philosophy, ascension</keywords>

--- Page 318 ---
<meta>This page concludes the first part of the treatise, finishing a discussion on the transformative properties of different "fires" and summarizing the natural formation of minerals.</meta>

...copper. If the lower hot fire does not accomplish it, then surely the cold fire must do so, for it dissolves again into its mercury—which is the <term>flux</term><note>original: "flux"; here referring to the state of being fluid or the substance that promotes melting</note> of the cold fire. If the fire takes hold of it, then it must run to all bodies; in its running, it sheds not only the lowermost but the uppermost body as well. Take this into further consideration.

## CHAP. XLIX.

### Of the warm fire.

I have spoken of this already; it can be created and controlled in several ways. Coals, wood, pitch, oil, and other combustible things are suitable for it. Here, I only wish to speak of a heat that is good for the melting of metals, by which they are purified, as you heard above; there is no need to repeat it here.

This concludes the first part, where I have provided information about the <term>nether work</term><note>The natural geological processes occurring deep within the earth, as opposed to the "upper work" of the alchemist’s lab.</note> or preliminary work governed and observed by nature, through which she presents metals and minerals to us in their various forms. He who correctly understands and reflects upon this work operates with advantage and usefulness; it is a great help toward proceeding successfully in <term>Alchemy</term>, which imitates and follows in nature's footsteps. I heartily wish success to all those who have an affection and love for this study.

# CHAP. III.

## Concerning the stones, rocks, and flints of gold, its formation <note>original: "operation"</note>, characteristics, and patterns of occurrence <note>original: "striking courses"</note>.

**G**old is formed in its proper rocks and marbles, and in the purest source <note>original: "matrix"</note> of the solid earth. It is composed of a most perfect <term>salt</term>, <term>Sulphur</term>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>These three elements—salt, sulfur, and mercury—were known in alchemy as the *Tria Prima*, the fundamental components of all matter.</note>, purified from all waste <note>original: "feces"</note> and impure spirits. This occurs through the union of a naturally highly purified "heavenly" state, consisting of white, yellow, and red sulfurous earth, following the fiery nature of *Sol* <note>Sol refers to the Sun, which alchemists associated with gold.</note> in a state of deep stability <note>original: "fixation"</note>.

Consequently, no other metal has a more elevated, compact, or heavier body than gold. It is a golden substance entirely free of moisture <note>original: "humidity"</note>. All the elements are equally bound together within it; in their unity, they have created such a stable body, colored throughout with an eternal lemon-yellow <note>original: "citrin"</note> hue. This is achieved through the strongest bond and union of its pure earth, <term>Sulphur</term>, and <term>Mercury</term>. With its <term>Vitriol essence</term> <note>Vitriol was a term for various sulfate minerals, often seen as a powerful transformative substance in alchemy.</note>, gold performs the same functions on earth that the Sun performs among the stars.

Naturally, everything that attaches to it on all sides is gold. It is found within the finest and most tightly packed stones and mineral veins <note>original: "passages"</note>. The power of *Sol* acts purely upon that ore <note>original: "oar"</note>, and in its quality, the ore is comparable to the Sun itself. This noble gold stone and ore is sometimes mixed with other substances; on its exterior, some dark and murky matter may cling to it, having "seed-like" matter <note>original: "spermatick matter," referring to the alchemical belief that metals grew from "seeds" or vapors within the earth.</note> or flat fragments attached to it. This detracts from its inherent goodness. And although the Creator has endowed it with great powers <note>original: "Vertues"</note>, it remains humble and allows itself to be

[Gold is] found in worthless <note>original: "despicable"</note> mineral stones, where it loses much of its color <note>original: "tincture"</note>, as is apparent by the touchstone <note>A dark stone used to test the purity of precious metals by the color of the streak they leave behind.</note>, where the mixture of copper, silver, tin, and others is seen. All these mixed impurities can be separated from it with technical processes <note>original: "artificial Manuals"</note>, and with little effort, it may be brought into a perfect state. Gold ores <note>original: "oars"</note> are naturally formed so that the gold sits within them closely, compactly, firmly, and purely, which is sometimes found in the cross-veins <note>original: "cross passages"</note>. Its stability <note>original: "fixedness"</note> is found deep underground, where it has its greatest power. It is also sometimes found in a speckled jasper <note>original: "jaspis"</note>, full of "eyes" <note>circular, eye-like patterns in the stone</note>, and mixed with flints in its veins, where vitriol flint is often found abundantly. This vitriol <note>A sulfate mineral, highly valued in alchemy for its acidic and metallic properties.</note> is the best among all other types of vitriols. 

The *Hungarian* vitriol takes precedence over all the rest, which is well known through their tests and examinations, as can be clearly demonstrated to the eye. In these veins, colorful fluxes <note>Minerals or substances used to promote the melting and purification of metals.</note> are sometimes found, which are interspersed <note>original: "interclined"</note> with gold and must be extracted using fire. For that purpose, it is necessary to treat it with the kind of fire you heard about in the first part. Commonly, *Zwitters* <note>A German mining term for tin-ore or complex mixed ores.</note> and *Zirn* stones are of this type; they must be stamped, beaten, reduced to a fine powder <note>original: "drawn to a narrowness"</note>, and refined.

Gold is also formed in vertical veins <note>original: "standing passages"</note> and on level ground. The ores and these veins are yellowish, rocky, and composed of iron-rich sand; it grows compactly in crevices <note>original: "clifts"</note>. Generally, it is found near flint-works. Sometimes it is found in flint, or in a liver-colored jasper, and sometimes in white pebbles. The gold found within these is of a white color, like silver, or found in white-copper ore.

In flinty, glittering passages it is found hoary and compactly formed. There are also found flat marble "floats" <note>ore deposits found near the surface or in horizontal beds</note>, wherein gold is wrought into all your crevices, mixed with green grit and iron spots. Sometimes it is also found in square iron shots <note>pellets or small crystalline cubes of iron ore</note>, or porous marble marcasites <term>Marcasite: a mineral (iron sulfide) often mistaken for gold; "fool's gold"</term>; but for the most part it is found in grits. Sometimes gold ore is also found compact and firm in black passages. Some gold ores and gold passages are also found to be composed of minerals and vitriol <term>Vitriol: a metal sulfate, often found where ores are weathering</term>, and miners in *Hungary* especially can speak of this, because gold ore is found in that manner in those parts.

# Basilius Valentinus: His Last Will and Testament

A naturally fitted stone produces silver ore <note>original: "oar"</note>, following its heavenly influence and the nocturnal influences of the Moon. In northern regions, the most abundant silver veins <note>original: "passages"</note> are found; for just as the Moon <note>original: *Luna*</note> borrows her light from the Sun <note>original: *Sol*</note>, silver veins and silver stones have gold veins at their right side. With that noble Queen, *Lunaria* <note>A name for silver in alchemy, often associated with the moon-herb moonwort</note>, a root is compared, by which the gold veins acquire strength and gain more power in that mixture, obtaining their ores from their roots.

Ancient philosophers wrote strangely of Virtue <note>here meaning a specific inherent power or property</note> as a fertile companion to the Sun <note>original: *Sol*</note>. This may be applied to both the upper and lower metallic work, because next to gold, nothing is as stable <note>original: "fix"</note> as silver is in its perfection. The reason silver veins are accompanied by white fluxes and mineral veins is that adjacent to them are the passages in which red mineral-sulfur and the reddish-yellow juices of noble gold are generated.

Silver metallic ore is often formed with a reddish-gold tint and emerges better than other types—a fact that can be proven if the process is well-ordered. White gold ore is naturally tinted this way by white copper glass <note>likely an arsenical copper or a specific vitreous mineral</note>, which produces such ores and veins by "feeding" their perfect minerals. Along with the glass ore, black fumes are exhaled which feed upon bismuth <note>original: "Wismuth"</note>, lead, and tin ore. In these ores, minerals that occur near the lunar <note>silver-related</note> veins are greedily refreshed. 

In this way, the firmest and most compact silver ore grows from its pure, proper, and unmixed stone, improving <note>original: "meliorating"</note> the poor areas and materials. Next to gold, silver ore has many remarkable virtues derived from heavenly influences; these influences transform several sorts of silver stones as they descend from the origins of their highest, finished unity.

This metallic ore is often found in flat float-works which consist of green flint. Many times it appears in a red or brown form, and it is also seen like limestone in black and yellow flat-works. Ironstone also receives the more noble metals—Gold, Silver, Copper, Tin, and Lead—which can make it difficult to process. However, gold and silver are not harmful to it; they make it malleable. ### *Of Tin: Its ore, operation, mist, stocks, floats, fallings, and striking passages.*

**T**in ore is formed in sandstone, receiving its influence from Jupiter <note>In alchemy, the planet Jupiter is traditionally associated with the metal tin</note> above. All these incorporate together to form the body of **Tin**. This harmful fume is the cause of the brittleness of **Tin**, and it makes all other metals that are melted with it harmful and brittle. This **Tin** or **Zwitter** <note>A German mining term for tin-stone or cassiterite</note> grows or breaks in a threefold manner: it slides, it is full of fumes, and it grows in pieces. ## CHAPTER IX.
### *Concerning Mercury ore and its veins,*

**M**ercury ore is formed in its characteristic host rocks <note>original: mine-stones</note> by the quality of its salt earth and its nimble, volatile earth. It exists in a moist, greasy, slimy, watery oiliness <term>original: oleity</term> which is mixed with a most subtle, red, sulfurous <note>original: sulphureous</note>, refined <note>original: digested; in alchemy, "digestion" refers to the process of maturing or refining a substance through slow, gentle heat</note> earth, with a very weak flowing bond, like an unripe, pleasing fruit of all specific metals.

Mercury shows its power in many things admirably, and works effectively upon minerals and metallic sulfur, and upon those substances which border upon antimony stones or ores. It loves to be in such places where the tin ores lie higher than the silver veins <note>original: passages</note>. It requires many repeated, effective operations upon other ores, and is multiplied upon other strange stones; it is drawn through the mineral juices <note>Early modern naturalists believed metals grew from liquid "juices" circulating in the earth.</note> and metals which have an affinity for one another, and produces many strange hybrids <note>original: miscreants; here referring to impure or mixed mineral forms</note>. This is the reason why it is so compatible with metals; goldsmiths use it to amalgamate <term>the process of mixing mercury with another metal, such as gold, to form an alloy</term> and for gilding.

It is also used for metallic colors, and is processed into oils and waters for human health. It is sublimated <term>the process of heating a substance into vapor and then cooling it back to solid form to purify it</term> to neutralize <note>original: corrode; here meaning to break down or counteract</note> the worst of poisons. It is a true thief <note>original: Robber; referring to mercury’s ability to dissolve and "steal" other metals into itself</note>, taking along whatever costs have been bestowed on him; but if he can be caught in his true nature, then he is in subjection and obedience to both the living and the dead. He is very effective in medicine, especially for external sores; he is bad for the bad, and good for the good, and is not everyone's friend, even though he is willing.

## CHAPTER 11.

### THE
# THIRD PART
### IS
## A Declaration of the
# Twelve Keys
<note>original: XII. Keyes</note>

**H**ere follows the third part of my intended writings, in which is truly shown the original and primary matter of our philosophical stone <term>Philosophical Stone: a legendary alchemical substance said to be capable of turning base metals into gold and serving as an elixir of life</term>. This provides a perfect instruction for the practical application, showing the direct way to the inexhaustible fountain of health and the abundance of riches to provide for human necessities. This is a declaration of my former writings, left as a token of affection for all those who are lovers of philosophy.

My friend, you must note that in this intended work concerning minerals, I had reason to include the two preceding parts on minerals, metals, and their ores <note>original: "Oars"</note>, as I considered it a necessity to hold...

### *An Elucidation of the XII. Keys.*

...bringing forth a light to the uninformed, showing how a single spirit from above forms all such ores <note>original: Oars</note>, metals, and minerals, originating underground in order to generate there. For the earth is always ready and eager to attract and retain that spirit which proceeds from the powers of the heavens, which it eventually brings to form and perfection. The way this happens has been discussed enough in my previous writings, which is why I only give hints about them here.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Note that all things originate from a heavenly influence, elemental operation, and earthly substance. From this mixture arise the four elements—water, air, and earth—which create through the help of the fire hidden within them in a warm digestion <note>an alchemical term for the process of heating a substance slowly over time</note>, producing a soul, spirit, and body. These are the three primary principles, which through coagulation <note>the process of a liquid thickening or becoming solid</note> become Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt. When these three are joined, they produce a perfect body according to the nature of the seed, whether it belongs to the mineral, animal, or vegetable kingdom. All things in the world that can be seen or felt are divided into these three kingdoms: the Animal kingdom, which contains those that have the breath of life and are composed of flesh and blood, such as humans, beasts, worms, fish, and birds; the Vegetable kingdom, which contains trees, herbs, seeds, roots, fruits, and everything that has the quality of growth; and the Mineral kingdom, which contains all kinds of ores, metals, minerals, marcasites <note>a mineral similar to pyrite or "fool's gold"</note>, calamines <note>original: Calves; likely referring to calamine, a zinc ore</note>, zincs, cobalts <note>original: Cobol's</note>, all sorts of flints, pebbles, bismuths <note>original: wismuths</note>, and stones, both precious and common.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Animals have their own specific seed, a spermatic substance, which after mating generates flesh...

Vegetables also have their own seed which God bestowed on them according to their various qualities and forms by a heavenly and sidereal <term>sidereal: relating to the stars or celestial influence</term> influence. They receive their elemental, fruitful growth from the earth in an orderly way, so that they may generate and increase.

Minerals and metals also have their original seed from God, through the influence of the heavens in a liquid, airy substance. This is composed of a mineral spirit, a sulfurous soul, and an earthly salt joined in one body; I have spoken of these in my earlier writings.

Note further: if any of these metallic and mineral types are to be brought to a further propagation and increase, they must be reduced back to their first seed and *first matter* <note>original: *prima materia*</note>.

If you wish to transmute metals, increase them, or bring them into a tincture or the *Philosopher’s Stone* <note>original: *Philosophick stone*</note>, you must first understand how you may destroy the metallic and mineral form through the spagyric <term>spagyric: the alchemical art of separating and then recombining the constituent parts of a substance</term> art. You must separate it into Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt. These three must be purely separated and brought back to their first principles.

This separation is performed in and by a Mercurial spirit, a sulfurous soul, and a white salt. Through the correct management of a true manual process, these three must be joined again so that they may be brought to the highest and most perfect purity.

# An Elucidation of the XII. Keys.

...heavenly, then the elemental, and lastly the earthly qualities are enclosed and lie hidden within it.

For the Mercurial spirit is cold and moist, the sulfurous <note>original: "sulphureous"</note> Soul is warm and dry. This liquid is the true first matter <note>original: *prima materia*</note> and the first seed of metals and minerals. Through the art of fire <note>original: *Vulcans* Art</note>, it is brought to a state beyond <note>original: *pluſquam*</note> perfection—a transcendent, stable <note>original: "fix'd"</note> medicine. From this, the true Philosopher's Stone is generated and must be produced in this manner.

Therefore, observe and take notice that all metals and minerals have only *one root* from which they generally descend. He who knows this rightly does not need to destroy metals to extract the Spirit from one, the Sulfur from a second, and the Salt from a third. There is a more direct source where these three—Spirit, Soul, and Body—lie hidden together in a single thing. This source is well known and may be obtained with great merit; it will be named later using several different terms.

<margin>5th Key</margin>
He who learns to know exactly this golden seed, or this *Magnet*, and searches thoroughly into its properties, then possesses the true root of life and may attain what his heart longs for. In my former writings, as well as in the **Twelve** <note>original: **XII.**</note> **Keys** from the first to the last, I arranged my writing style to present to future generations the practical method <note>original: *practick*</note> for making the great Philosopher's Stone or the best purified gold. This is done using Sulfur and Salt with the help of the spirit of Mercury, which must be drawn from a crude, unmelted mineral ore <note>original: *Minera*</note>, according to the meaning of my fifth Key, which was set down as a parable.

<header># An Explanation of the Twelve Keys.</header>

...and of the primary planetary colors, and their final purpose. After accomplishing these, study the ***Twelve Keys*** carefully, for each contains a specific process.

The first Key informs you that if you seek for the "seed" within a **metallic body**, such as **gold**, then before anything else, it must be thoroughly purged of all its impure "leprosy" <note>original: "leprosie"; a common alchemical term for the impurities or base elements mixed with a noble metal</note>. Furthermore, nothing must be mixed with our **fountain** <note>original: "Fountain"; likely referring to the primary solvent or the base material in its liquid state</note> except that which is of a pure generative <note>original: "spermatick"</note> quality. 

This purification is performed with **antimony**, which has a close relationship and affinity to **gold**. This is why antimonial sulfur purges the **soul of gold**, refining <note>original: "graduating"</note> it to a very high degree. Conversely, gold can quickly improve the **soul of antimony** and bring it to a firm state of stability <term>fixation</term>. This exalts both antimony and gold to an equal status and power. They can be transformed not only into a white metal like **silver** <note>original: "Lune"</note> but also into a transcendent **medicine** for human health, about which you will receive further instructions later when I discuss antimony specifically. 

Although antimony has promised a friendly brotherhood to **lead** <note>original: "Saturn"</note>—because antimony’s properties are somewhat similar to lead’s in an equal harmony—once the exalted **sulfur of antimony** is stabilized, its former friend lead can no longer take anything from it. This is because the **King** (gold) has received it into his golden palace and made it a partner in his triumphant kingdom. This is why it can now endure both heat and cold and overcome them, standing with the King as a **conqueror** in great and transcendent glory.

Laminate the gold thinly in the proper manner, melt it three times with antimony, and afterward the *regulus* <note>original: "Regulus"; the metallic mass that sinks to the bottom of the crucible during smelting</note> which is produced by the melting must be melted with a bellows in a strong fire and refined with lead <note>original: "Saturn"; the alchemical name for lead</note>. Then you will find the purest, most beautiful, and most lustrous gold, as pleasant to behold as the brilliance of the sun <note>original: "Sol"</note>. This gold is now prepared to surrender its innermost essence; being first changed from its solid state into a form that can be broken down, it passes through the "salt-sea" of its own decomposition, is submerged within it, emerges again, and appears visibly.

### An Elucidation of the XII. Keys.

...you shall hear, it is brought into an *amalgam* <note>original: "Amalgama"; a mixture of mercury with another metal.</note> of *mercury* and of *sulfur*, which immediately seizes on him <note>The "King," representing Gold.</note>, corrodes all his parts, and is dissolved; it is then immediately transformed <note>original: "mortified"</note> by this salt-water <note>Likely a reference to a corrosive acid like *aqua regia*.</note> into a most splendid, transparent oil. 

You must note, however, that this dissolution is not sufficient. The King is not yet minded to let go of his soul out of his fixed body—which you can see when you separate the water from the dissolved body of the King—where you shall find a fixed powder of gold, out of which you will hardly extract the soul that remains within. 

Therefore, follow my counsel and bear the yoke which I bore before you, and learn to know exactly through hard work how to proceed further, as I shall inform you. Having dissolved your gold wholly in the said water and brought it into a pleasant yellow oil, then let it stand well <term>luted</term> <note>sealed with an airtight clay or wax sealant</note> for a day and night in a very gentle <term>Balneum Mariae</term> <note>a "Bath of Mary," or a gentle water bath used for indirect heating</note>. The <term>feces</term> <note>original: "feces"; the dregs or sediment that settle at the bottom</note> which have settled must be separated from it. 

Then take this pure dissolution and put it into a well-coated body, or <term>retort</term> <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note>. Apply a helmet <note>The top part of a still, also known as an alembic.</note> to it, with a receiver attached and luted in the best manner. Set it into a sand <term>capel</term> <note>a sand bath used for even heating</note> and drive the gold with the water over the helmet. Repeat <note>original: "iterate"</note> this a third time; then remove the water in the *Balneum Mariae*. You will find a beautiful gold powder. Keep this in a glass for an hour in the fire, so that the remaining humidity may be drawn from it.

Let the gold become increasingly volatile until, at last, the entire substance passes over. Through this repeated distillation, its fixed body is divided, all its members are torn apart and opened, and it willingly yields its soul to a special judge, about which my third key will give sufficient information.

Note further that after this work, those salt spirits must be removed <note>original: "abstracted"</note> from the gold that was distilled over. Gold and silver—but chiefly gold—are brought to the highest degree of fixedness <term>original: "fixedness"; the state of a substance that is stable and does not evaporate or change when exposed to fire</term> by such degrees as nature provided. Indeed, its nature is found to be very hot and fiery, freed from all phlegmatic humidity <note>original: "phlegmatick humidity"; an excess of watery or cool moisture associated with the element of water</note>. Silver <note>original: "Lune"</note> is not so wholly freed from this moisture, though she has obtained a degree of fixed sulfur and waits for the King <note>Gold</note> to warm her cold body with his hot seed. This concerns the specific details of the process and will be plainly demonstrated in its proper place. In gold, there is no watery humidity at all, unless it were reduced again into vitriol <note>original: "Vitriol"; a sulfate of a metal; here referring to a salt or liquid form of gold</note>. This would be a useless and unprofitable work and would require huge expenses if the Philosopher’s Stone were to be made of the vitriol of gold, for one would need a great store of it. Indeed, in that vitriol, one would find a suitable spirit that nature would desire, of a white quality, as well as a Soul and Salt of a glorious essence.

But regarding what countries, goods, and lands have been ruined <note>original: "dilapidated"</note> this way, I decline to speak. I only give this warning to my disciples: since nature has left a nearer way to follow and imitate, they should take heed not to fall into such extreme and inescapable <note>original: "inextricable"</note> poverty.

The solar mercury <note>Gold in its mercury form</note> is never brought so far toward destruction <note>total chemical breakdown</note>, nor did the ancient philosophers ever use that way, as it is a thing completely contrary to nature. It does indeed contain a humidity, but it is a mere elemental watery humidity after its dissolution and is good for nothing. ...the principles and seeds of metals, which I have spoken of previously. Therefore, let no one be so overly clever as to try to make our Stone <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> only from dry and fully digested gold. This is because its "phlegmatic humidity" <note>In alchemy, this refers to the watery or volatile principle within a substance</note> has already entered into a dry state of stability and fixed coagulation. This is not the case with other metals; although they are also subject to a hard coagulation and have passed through the fire, they are not yet wholly digested <note>original: "digested"; in alchemy, this refers to the process of maturation through heat</note>, nor brought to full maturity from their natural, original root. This should be taken into account, and do not be offended by my earlier writings if they seem to contradict this.

Although I have shown that the Spirit, Soul, and Body all come from one metallic essence and must be prepared this way—among which I held gold to be the best—I acted in this matter as seemed fit for a philosopher. The ancient philosophers did the same before me, but I hope you noticed my disclaimer <note>original: "protestation"</note>: that I specifically intended to spark your own contemplation <note>original: "speculation"</note> so that you might better observe nature and its principles and consider its origin. It was not appropriate for me to inform everyone how the doors are bolted within—especially at a time when I never intended to write so plainly about these things, which are hidden even from the best of men. However, when my "heavenly Prince" <note>Likely referring to a divine command or spiritual revelation</note> commanded me and changed my mind, he told me not to bury the talent I had been given, but to share it with those whom God deems worthy. I must remind you of one more rule regarding the points I set down previously, which I have just spoken of, so that you will be less likely to blame me or think I am now rejecting what I formerly wrote.

### An Elucidation of the XII. Keys.

Read through everyone who has written about metals since the beginning of the world, and you will find that they were all of one mind, and that **I** make use of their sayings: that the first and the last metal is a metal. This is because the first metal has already obtained and acquired the developing seed of metals in a metallic quality <term>original: Metalline quality; the inherent nature or "essence" that allows a substance to grow into a metal</term>. This quality does nothing else but proceed incessantly in the generation of metals, as **I** spoke of in the first and second parts of *Minerals and Metals*, and as **I** have also mentioned in several places in this current part.

Many have called gold "lead," and lead they called "gold." This was not only because they were found to have the same weight <note>original: ponderousness</note>, but because three deep, glittering stones have solely received their transcendent perfection from this planet <note>In alchemy, planets correspond to metals; "this planet" refers to Saturn, which is associated with Lead</note>. There are many other causes besides, but to relate them here would be too long and unnecessary. This is the matter which requires wisdom to distinguish—to look into these and other things and to search exactly into God's mysteries and the nature laid before us. But because humanity has been brought to a deep blindness through Adam's fall, our understanding is so eclipsed that we can hardly conceive of this or other mystical matters in nature.

The stubbornness <note>original: obduration</note> among the greedy is so great that most of them search and dive into such mysteries out of mere covetousness, pride, and ambition. This led the ancient philosophers—acting upon the command and inspiration of the Highest—to set a certain limit to their efforts and to write of such mysteries in such a manner that unworthy men should not understand them; only worthy men, through their spiritual illumination, might

...perceive it. By writing often about one thing, they have mixed others in, while still meaning one and the same thing. In several places, they showed that the Philosopher's Stone is and comes from an animal seed; others say it comes from a vegetable seed; and a third sort says it comes from a mineral seed. Others write that the stone is made of animal, vegetable, and mineral seeds together. All of this is only understood as the mineral and metallic <term>metalline</term> seed, and does not consist of a plurality of seeds. 

Because of this, the Art became obscured, so much so that scarcely one in many thousands attains knowledge of it. For that reason, it is held to be a secret Art, so that not every dunce should get it into his thick head <note>original: "Beetle-head," a common term for a dull or stupid person</note>. And why should he? For if this Art were as common as brewing beer or baking bread, then anyone may judge what good could be expected. Would not all kinds of vices be practiced publicly without any control?

Therefore, such men who, in their haughty minds, are only interested in pomp and pride, must have their wings clipped; these things ought not to be put into their mouths. These matters are clear enough for those upon whom God intends to bestow them.

I return now to the thing I intended, which is to teach an eager student how to proceed further with the extracted Soul of Gold. Truly, it is a great thing to discover such mysteries; I warn everyone to make good use of them. Note that if you have the purple mantle of *Sol* <note>Sol refers to the Sun, the alchemical symbol for Gold</note>, such as the sulfur of *Sol*, then be thankful to God for it. Bear no evil mind against your neighbor, and unlock your golden seed according to the meaning of the...

As you heard before, the whole mystery lies herein, namely, in the tinging of red fiery spirits of metallic souls; and everything that is tinged red, and is known to have a fierce sulfur—all such are related to the *Solar Astrum* <note>original: "Solar Astrum," likely referring to the spiritual essence or "star" of gold</note>. Such souls and gold-like *sulfurs* are found most effectively in *Mars* <note>iron</note> and *Venus* <note>copper</note>, as well as in *vitriol* <note>sulfate minerals</note>. With little effort and in a short time, each can be extracted from it separately, as you shall hear when I give a further account of the *mineral vitriol* that is mined in *Hungary* and is of a high grade.

Now, if you have wit and understanding, and are inclined and heartily desire to conceive the true meaning of my *Keys* and of my other writings—thereby to unlock the secrets of metals for our benefit—then you should have noticed and observed that in all these, I have written not only of the metal of *Sol* <note>gold</note>, its *sulfur*, and its *salt*, but I have also inserted and mixed in other red metals, making them uniform, from which the *mystical mastery* <term>the successful completion of the alchemical Great Work</term> may be obtained. For this purpose, I took great pains to disclose that which the whole world kept silent about, concealed until their final moments, and buried in silence in their very graves.

My goal in doing so was not to seek any vain glory, but rather that God’s gracious and provident goodness might be revealed to posterity. # To the Reader.

If we reflect on former ages and consider how few people employed themselves in the scrutiny of the secret mysteries <note>original: *Arcanums*</note> of Nature, we realize how destitute the philosophers of those times were of the helps and advantages we enjoy for correctly understanding such mysteries. Hermes, the "Prince of Philosophers," seemed to stand alone as the only inventor of this most excellent art <note>Alchemy, often called the "Hermetic Art" after Hermes Trismegistus.</note>.

Cremer, the Abbot and our countryman, after thirty years of study and expensive practice and labor, was compelled to seek a master in Italy. Flamel the Parisian <note>original: *Lutetian*; referring to Nicolas Flamel of Paris.</note> suffered the same hard fortune, along with many other of the ancients. Our author, Basil <note>original: *Basilius*; referring to the legendary alchemist Basil Valentine.</note>, confesses that he would never have attained the knowledge of this art if, by God's special grace, some books of the ancient masters had not come into his hands.

Have we not cause, then, to bless God that we live in such an age, and in such a nation also, where we may converse with many philosophers, both ancient and modern? These are men whose works show them to be servants to the Most High, beloved by Him, and acquainted with the most occult and secret mysteries and wonders <note>original: *Arcanums*</note> of Nature. Having toiled and spent much of their precious time in fruitless labors, they have—to prevent the same in their successors—discovered and, as it were, chalked <note>The catchword "ed" on the original page indicates the word continues as "chalked."</note>

<summary>In this preface, the author argues that modern seekers are fortunate to have access to many alchemical texts and masters, unlike the ancient philosophers who often spent decades searching for knowledge in isolation.</summary>

## The Preface.

I considered it my conscientious duty to be reconciled in a *Christian* way with my fellow members who are currently alive, and with those who are to follow in future ages. I do this so that my *soul* may be at rest, patiently waiting for the *Lord's* call to become an inhabitant of that heavenly *Paradise* and to be enrolled in the Book of Life, standing in readiness day and night to watch for my *Lord's* coming. In consideration of this, I recall the writings which I set down on paper—as other ancient *philosophers* have done before me—publishing all those mysteries of nature through which practitioners <note>original: "Artists"</note> and those who feel affection and love for such mystical truths may benefit. I lovingly and readily leave these things to them, just as the highest <term>Spagyrist</term> <note>original: "Spagyrick"; an alchemist who practices the art of separating and recombining natural elements</note> and heavenly *Physician* has granted and revealed them to me. 

My conscience has further urged me, in the pursuit of *Christian* love and the performance of my promise dictated by nature, to provide a more detailed account. I believe it is appropriate and necessary to set forth the *handbooks* <note>original: "Manuals"</note> belonging to this study, which ought to be described in detail to fully inform the judgment of men devoted to this work. Specifically, I will show how nature's bolts—which she has slid forward in various ways to strongly lock away her secrets—are to be pushed back, so that the doors of worldly *treasures* might be unlocked. In this way, the knowledge of transcendent mysteries may be attained, and through serious, continued prayers to the *Creator*, human judgment and understanding might be further encouraged <note>original: "egg’d on"</note>.

I am not compelled by force or poverty <note>original: "indigency"</note>, nor by vanity or self-interest, to write down any word and leave it to posterity. My only motivation is a mere consideration of the frailty and misery of this world, where the *children* of darkness are almost entirely lost in their

They describe alchemy as a divine gift from God (the "highest Spagyrist") intended to unlock nature's hidden treasures through study and prayer.</summary>
<keywords>alchemy, Spagyrick, philosophy, Christian duty, Book of Life, secrets of nature, divine revelation, manuals</keywords>

# The Preface.

...groping ways, has caused me to do so. I cannot express how much my mind is troubled when I think on the folly of this frail world and consider the Cimmerian darkness <note>original: "Cymmerian darkness"; a reference to the Cimmerians of Greek mythology, who were said to live in perpetual mist and darkness; here it means total ignorance.</note> of its children. They think themselves to be of deep understanding when they have heard some nonsense from their **university professors** <note>original: "University Chair-men"</note> discussed, thereby supposing themselves to be much enlightened in their understandings. 

Where is that high and precious *Medicine* of the ancient *Philosophers* <note>In this context, "medicine" refers to the Universal Medicine or Philosopher's Stone sought by alchemists to cure both metals and the human body.</note> who lived before any *university* was talked or heard of? They received their *revelations* through earnest, pious prayer to *God*, joining to it their daily searching into natural things and applying their hands to the work. Where, I ask, has their diligence <note>original: "painfulness"</note> and industry fled? Surely to no other place than to the horrid, impure, and filthy *apothecary shops* <note>Early modern pharmacies where drugs were prepared and sold; the author views them as corruptions of true alchemy.</note>—deeply cast down and buried in the earth, sunk so deep that neither the ringing of bells nor the beating of mortars is able to rouse it. Thus, their praise and the glory of the Highest is at a standstill! And who produces any good from it? 

I am convinced of this: that if my writings shall be brought to light after my death, and if a wise posterity and their disciples rightly read, meditate upon, and understand them well—seeking, diving into, and working the same out of a *Christian* intention only for the glory of *God* and the love and charity of their fellow brothers and *Christians*—then by means of their actions and works (which depend on such good and proper fundamentals), all those foolish and forged claims will be discovered and exposed to public view. ## The Preface.

No man is able to outrun a good intention; do not let your greedy mind dwell on how you may obtain an abundance of gold, silver, riches, and vanity. Instead, before everything else written here, let your chief aim be how you may be helpful in word and deed to promote the health of your fellow Christian. If you do this, you have given and brought an offering of thanks, and God will bestow more upon you; such revelations will come to you, more than you would have ever believed.

Therefore, instead of a perfect book of medicine <note>original: "Physick book"</note>, I have added at the end those precious medicines with which, even to this hour, I have successfully cured many difficult symptoms and diseases held by others to be incurable. I recommend these to you, along with the rest of the things contained in these writings, charging your conscience to be wary and not to abuse any of them—as much as your life and soul are near and dear to you.

If you receive this faithful admonition <note>a firm warning or piece of advice</note> and warning, which I give to you here and there at the beginning, middle, and end, and in other places also, and act accordingly, then you cannot be too thankful for these things which—through God’s permission—shall be suggested and made known to you from this book.

But if you strive against my faithful warning and fatherly advice, or if you allow these mysteries—which were hidden from the learned—to fall into the wrong <note>original: "strange"</note> hands, look out for yourself! Do not blame me, and do not think there is any reconciliation for you, as you will be cut off from all those who live and die in Christ.

Thus I let it rest, committing the judgment <note>original: "execution"</note> to the Highest, who dwells in Heaven, and who punishes and avenges all manner of sin, vice, and iniquity...
